Flip tops within a premium range

Collections rarely run one build, and the Custom Gift Boxes range covers the lidded, drawer and magnetic formats a flip-top sits beside. Sharing one wrap and one print system across them means a range reads as a family even when the openings differ.

What to send with your enquiry

The contents and their weight, and roughly how often the box will be opened over its life. The first sets the board and insert; the second sets the wrap, which is what determines whether the hinge lasts.

Lead times, and why rigid cannot be rushed

Rigid boxes are wrapped in a largely manual operation, and a flip-top adds the hinge to that. Lead times run noticeably longer than folding cartons, which matters most on seasonal ranges where a late delivery has nowhere to go.

The usual approach is to order against the season rather than against demand, with a plain wrap that a printed sleeve or a label can adapt if the range shifts. That keeps the long-lead component decided early and the fast-moving decisions late.

Shipping assembled

A rigid flip-top cannot be flat-packed, so it ships formed and takes several times the volume of a folding equivalent. On a long freight leg that can outweigh the difference in unit price, and nesting sizes where the range allows it recovers a useful part of that.

Choose Kraft Flip Top Rigid Boxes from Kraft Box Pack, with the hinge specified rather than assumed. We provide:

  • Gloss, matte, and spot UV coating options

  • Free design and free shipping

  • Magnetic, friction and tab catches on one build

  • Food-safe and eco-friendly kraft material

  • Fast turnaround times at wholesale rates

Send the contents and how often the box gets opened and we will specify the wrap from both.

description:
Kraft Flower Boxes, Built for Water and Weight

Flower packaging is the only gift format that has to hold something wet and living. Stems in floral foam or a water source make the base damp from the moment the arrangement is built, and board loses strength as it takes up moisture. At Kraft Box Pack we line and reinforce Kraft Flower Boxes from the base up, because that is where they fail.

Whether you are sourcing flower boxes wholesale for a florist or a delivery service, the decisions are the liner, the base construction and whether the arrangement travels standing or lying down.

Why the base decides everything

A liner, always

A plastic or waxed liner keeps water off the board. Without one the base softens within hours and gives way while being carried, which is the failure a customer remembers. Where recyclability matters, a removable liner keeps the box itself in the paper stream.

Weight of a wet arrangement

Soaked floral foam is heavy, and the weight sits entirely on a base that is simultaneously being softened by it. A full-overlap or double-thickness base carries that; a single glued seam does not, and it fails at the moment of lifting.

Height for the stems

Hat-box arrangements sit low, but a tied bouquet standing upright needs real height and a tapered shape so stems gather at the base and blooms open at the top. Measuring the arrangement rather than the flowers is what gets this right.

Travelling standing or lying

An arrangement carried upright by hand needs stability — a wide base and a low centre of gravity. One posted lying down needs the blooms held clear of the box walls and the water source sealed, which is a completely different build. Most florists doing both need two formats rather than one.

Key elements of flower box design

  1. A liner, so water never reaches the board.

  2. Full-overlap base, since wet foam is heavy and softening.

  3. Height measured to the arrangement, not the stems.

  4. Wide base for carrying, sealed source for posting.

  5. Ribbon or handle, because a wet box is awkward to grip.

Comparison with Kraft Candy Favor Boxes

Both are gift formats and only one has to survive being damp. Kraft Candy Favor Boxes are specified for presentation and a food barrier; a flower box is specified for water, weight and a base that is losing strength while it works. The two often appear in the same order and never in the same specification.

Print, and what damp does to it

Water and condensation lift some inks and coatings, and a box that looks perfect in a shop can be marked by the time it reaches a recipient. A water-based varnish or a matte laminate resists that; an uncoated print on the outside of a wet-lined box is asking for a mark exactly where the customer looks.

Foil holds up well on kraft here and does not care about damp, which is one reason so much floral packaging uses a single foil mark rather than colour.

Flower boxes within a gift range

Florists usually sell more than flowers, and the Custom Gift Boxes range covers the hamper, lidded and drawer builds that go alongside. Matching board and print across them is what makes an add-on look like part of the arrangement rather than a separate purchase.

What to send with your enquiry

Shapes, and what each one suits

Cylindrical hat boxes hold a domed arrangement well and are the most recognisable floral format, but they waste space in transit because circles do not pack tightly. Square and rectangular boxes ship far better and suit arrangements built to a flat top. Tapered boxes gather stems at the base and let blooms open above, which is why they suit tied bouquets specifically.

Most florists end up with two shapes rather than one, and the second is usually chosen for how it ships rather than how it looks.

Reuse, and why it matters here

Flower boxes are kept more than almost any gift packaging, because the recipient already has somewhere to put a nice box. That argues for a build that survives being emptied and dried out — a removable liner rather than a bonded one, and a base that does not delaminate once the water has gone.

faqs.answer: Kraft Flower Boxes are used to pack bouquets and floral gifts in a structured way so the arrangement stays stable during handling and delivery. faqs.question: What makes flower boxes better than simple wrapping?
faqs.answer: Simple wrapping protects the bouquet surface but does not control movement inside a shipping carton. A rigid flower box adds wall support and a stable base so the bouquet stays centered instead of sliding into corners. This reduces petal bruising, limits wrap creasing, and keeps the bouquet shape closer to the original arrangement on arrival.

faqs.question: Do you offer Kraft flower boxes wholesale ordering?
faqs.answer: Yes, Kraft flower boxes wholesale orders are common for florists, distributors, and gifting brands that need steady supply and consistent sizing. Wholesale runs are most effective when size range, lid style, and finish are set early so reorders match the previous batch. This helps maintain a consistent look across seasonal drops and daily bouquet programs.

faqs.question: What does Kraft flower boxes bulk mean in practical terms?
faqs.answer: Kraft flower boxes bulk usually means ordering quantities that support repeated bouquet packing over a season, promotion, or ongoing delivery schedule. Bulk planning focuses on storage efficiency, stacking strength, and repeatable packing routines. It also helps keep cost stable when the same size and structure are reordered regularly.

faqs.question: How do I choose the right size for bouquet boxes for flowers?
faqs.answer: Start by measuring the bouquet width and height with wrap, ribbon, and any padding included. Choose a box that gives controlled clearance so petals are not pressed while still limiting side drift. Testing the fullest bouquet size you sell helps prevent lids from tightening or catching on wrap edges during packing.

faqs.question: Are Flower boxes for arrangements suitable for tall bouquets?
faqs.answer: Yes, flower boxes for arrangements can be planned with extra depth so tall stems and lifted tops have space without contacting the lid. Depth planning is important because tall bouquets can create upward pressure on the lid if the box is too shallow. A stable base also helps tall bouquets stay upright rather than leaning.

faqs.question: What are Floral Boxes with Lids and why are they useful?
faqs.answer: Floral Boxes with Lids are flower packs that close over the bouquet to protect the top shape and keep wrap edges tucked. A lid helps reduce snagging during handling and keeps the outer box clean for gifting. Lidded styles also stack better in staging, which is useful when many orders are prepared for timed dispatch.

faqs.question: How do cardboard flower boxes wholesale runs stay consistent?
faqs.answer: Cardboard flower boxes wholesale runs stay consistent when one approved structure is reused with the same dielines, board strength, and lid fit. Consistency checks often include corner firmness, lid alignment in row stacking, and base flatness. Keeping the same carton layout also helps reduce corner rub during transit movement.

faqs.question: Can these boxes be used for retail counters and store pickup?
faqs.answer: Yes, these boxes work well for retail counters because they keep a tidy silhouette and support row displays. A stable lid line looks cleaner when many units are arranged together. For store pickup, the rigid build helps customers carry bouquets without squeezing petals or bending wrap folds.

faqs.question: Do you offer finishing options like Matte, Gloss, and Spot UV?
faqs.answer: Yes, Matte, Gloss, and Spot UV finishes can be selected depending on handling conditions and photo needs. Matte reduces glare and keeps the kraft tone calm under studio lighting. Gloss adds shine and can make printed areas appear stronger, while Spot UV adds controlled contrast on selected design areas.

faqs.question: How do finishes help during delivery and handling?
faqs.answer: Finishes help reduce visible rub marks that show on edges and corners during carton movement. A protective coating can also make the surface easier to keep clean during staging. When boxes move through courier handling, scuff control becomes important because the outer look affects gifting presentation on arrival.

faqs.question: Can Kraft Flower Boxes include inserts for stability?
faqs.answer: Yes, inserts like base pads and dividers can help keep bouquets centered and reduce movement. Inserts are useful when bouquets are heavy, when multiple items are packed together, or when add-ons like cards and small gifts need separation. The insert should hold items steady without squeezing petals or forcing the lid tight.

faqs.question: Are these boxes good for seasonal gifting and campaigns?
faqs.answer: Yes, they are often used for seasonal gifting because the same outer style can repeat across campaigns while artwork changes. A repeatable structure helps staff pack quickly during busy periods. It also keeps the brand presentation consistent across different bouquet types and seasonal promotions.

faqs.question: What should I share before placing an order?
faqs.answer: Share bouquet size range, typical wrap thickness, lid preference, quantity, and whether you need inserts or a window option. If printing is needed, share artwork and placement preferences for lid and front panels. Also share handling method, such as courier delivery or store pickup, because stacking and transit exposure affect build planning.

faqs.question: How do I reduce bouquet movement inside the box during transit?
faqs.answer: Use a close-fit size with controlled clearance and add a base pad or gentle side support if needed. Avoid oversized boxes that allow lateral drift into corners. Testing a short movement check with the fullest bouquet helps confirm that the bouquet stays centered and the lid closes flush without pressure.

description:
Kraft Food Boxes, Specified by What Goes Inside

Food packaging fails in one of three ways — grease comes through, moisture goes the wrong direction, or the box loses shape under a hot fill. Which of the three you are guarding against depends entirely on the dish, and it is the first thing worth deciding. At Kraft Box Pack we specify Kraft Food Boxes from the food outward rather than from a box size inward.

Whether you are sourcing kraft food boxes wholesale for a kitchen or comparing kraft food boxes with lids for a retail line, the useful starting point is the fill — dry, greasy, wet, hot or frozen — because each one points at a different board and a different barrier.

Barriers, and the recycling trade behind them

Grease

Fried and buttery foods need a grease-resistant treatment or the oil wicks through and stains the outside within minutes. The treatment can be a water-based coating that keeps the box recyclable, or a plastic laminate that does not. Both work; only one supports a recyclability claim on the pack.

Moisture, in both directions

Hot food gives off steam and cold food attracts condensation, and the two need opposite handling. A sealed box keeps sauce in and turns fried food soft; a vented one keeps it crisp and will not hold liquid. Where a menu has both, it usually needs two specifications rather than one compromise.

Heat and structure

Board softens as it absorbs heat and steam, so a box that holds shape cold can sag under a hot fill. Heavier caliper solves it, and so does a shorter time between fill and handover. Worth testing with the actual dish rather than assuming.

Food-safe is a specification, not a claim

Food contact means the board, the inks and the coating all have to be rated for it, not just the board. Direct contact and indirect contact have different requirements — a box holding a wrapped item is not the same as one the food sits in. Say which applies when you enquire and the grades are chosen accordingly. There is a fuller explanation in our note on food safe kraft packaging for bakeries and takeout.

Key elements of kraft food box design

  1. Barrier chosen for the fill, not applied by default.

  2. Vented or sealed, decided by whether the dish is fried or sauced.

  3. Caliper rated for a hot fill where one applies.

  4. Food-contact grades on board, ink and coating alike.

  5. Flat-packed, because kitchens have no storage.

Handles and the Kraft Gable Boxes option

Where the customer carries the food themselves, a handle changes the pack completely, and Kraft Gable Boxes are the format built around one. The handle has to be rated for a full load — a gable that tears under a hot meal is worse than no handle at all, because the failure happens while it is being carried.

Design considerations for kitchens and retail

Assembly time is a real cost. A box taking four seconds to build instead of one costs about an hour of labour across a busy service, so an auto-lock base that costs more per unit can still be cheaper overall. Time a sample by hand before committing to the run.

Print on kraft reads warm, so food photography shot on white board looks different on brown. Where the appetite appeal of an image matters, a white underbase holds the colour; without one, a warm-toned dish photographs better than a cool-toned one.

description:
Kraft Frozen Food Boxes, and Board at Minus Eighteen

A freezer is a hostile place for paperboard. Frost forms on every surface, the temperature cycles each time a door opens or a cabinet defrosts, and the water that condenses goes straight into any exposed fibre. At Kraft Box Pack a Kraft Frozen Food Box is specified as a moisture problem first, because that is what actually destroys these packs.

Not the cold. Board is perfectly happy cold. It is the water moving in and out of it, over and over, for months.

What repeated freezing does

Fibres swell and then split

Water absorbed into the board expands as it freezes, and it does that every cycle. Over a long storage life the layers begin to separate, and a delaminated carton loses most of its stiffness while looking almost normal from outside.

Print lifts at the edges

Ink and coating sit on a surface that is expanding and contracting underneath them. Without a proper barrier the print starts to lift along the score lines first, which is exactly where the eye lands.

Frost welds cartons together

Cartons packed damp and then frozen bond to each other, and pulling them apart tears the outer liner. A pack that goes into the cabinet dry is a pack that comes out separable.

Key elements of frozen carton design

  1. A moisture barrier specified as a board choice, not a print finish.

  2. Stacking strength assessed cold, since board behaves differently there.

  3. Ovenable board wherever the pack goes from freezer to oven.

  4. Storage, defrost and cooking instructions given real space.

  5. A shape that stands in a crowded upright freezer.

Frozen food is a dense, hard object

A frozen block has no give at all. Where a chilled product settles into a carton, a frozen one presses its corners into the same points for months and eventually pushes through a light board. It is also heavy for its volume, so a carton sized by appearance rather than by weight will bulge at the base and then stop stacking straight, which is how a whole facing goes untidy in a supermarket cabinet.

The freezer-to-oven question

If the pack goes into an oven, the board and every coating on it have to be rated for that, and the temperature and time have to be on the carton. This is a specification decision with no workaround: an ordinary coated board that is fine at minus eighteen can fail badly at two hundred, and it has to be declared before the material is bought rather than assumed from the artwork.

Comparison with Kraft Salad Boxes

Both are chilled food packs and the timescales could not be further apart. Kraft Salad Boxes hold a product for a day or two, so the pack manages appearance, ventilation and a little condensation. A frozen carton lives at low temperature for months with water cycling through it the whole time, which is a materials problem rather than a presentation one.

Vegetables and fruit Coated board Coated inner Light for its volume Months
Bakery and pastry Ovenable Coated inner Fragile when frozen Months

Standing up in a home freezer

Retail freezers are baskets and drawers, and at home the cabinet is packed. Cartons get stood on end, pushed sideways and buried, so a tall thin pack that presents beautifully on a shelf may be unusable in a drawer. A footprint that stands stably in either orientation is worth more here than a pack proportioned for a shelf edge, and it is worth checking against a real freezer drawer rather than a planogram.

Printing that survives the cabinet

Frozen cabinets are brightly lit and everything in them is behind a film of frost, so contrast matters more than detail. Fine type and subtle tonal work disappear behind ice within days. Strong type, clear product identification and a high-contrast panel are what remain readable, and on a brown kraft base that generally means keeping the palette narrow and letting the material do the rest.

Within a food packaging range

Frozen lines usually sit within a wider range that also runs chilled and ambient, and the Kraft Food Packaging collection covers those formats. One kraft stock and one design system across all three temperatures is what makes a brand recognisable in three different aisles.

The product's frozen weight, its intended shelf life, and whether the pack ever goes into an oven. The last answer changes the board entirely, so it is the one to settle first.

description:
Kraft Fruit Packaging Boxes, Built Around Ventilation

Fruit is alive after picking. It respires, giving off heat, moisture and ethylene, and packaging that traps any of the three shortens shelf life measurably. At Kraft Box Pack we specify Kraft Fruit Packaging Boxes from airflow first, because a sealed box is actively worse for fresh produce than an open one.

Whether you are sourcing fruit packaging boxes wholesale for a grower or a retail line, the decisions are vent area, stacking strength and how much the fruit bruises.

What Makes Kraft Right For Fresh Produce

Ventilation, and how much

Vent holes let heat and ethylene out and slow ripening. Too little and the box becomes a warm humid chamber; too much and the walls lose the strength holding a pallet up. Around five per cent of the wall area is the usual working figure, positioned so the holes line up when boxes are stacked — vents that are blocked by the box above achieve nothing.

Humidity, and what it does to board

Produce is stored damp and cold, and board absorbs moisture and loses stiffness as it does. A box rated for a stack in a dry warehouse can fail in a cold store, which is why produce cartons are specified with a moisture-resistant treatment and a caliper heavier than the weight alone suggests.

Bruising is a packaging failure

Soft fruit bruises from movement and from pressure, not from impact. Trays, cells and liners stop the movement; the right depth stops the fruit at the bottom carrying the weight of the fruit above it. Both are cheaper than the loss.

Stacking, because produce always does

Fruit boxes are stacked high on pallets and in cold stores, and the box at the bottom carries everything above it for the whole storage period, not just for a journey. Edge crush resistance is the figure that matters here, and it is the one that degrades most as board takes up moisture.

Key elements of fruit box design

  1. Vent area around five per cent, aligned between stacked boxes.

  2. Moisture-resistant treatment for cold, damp storage.

  3. Trays or cells on anything that bruises.

  4. Edge crush rated for the full stack, not a single box.

  5. Depth limited so lower fruit is not crushed by upper.

Comparison with Kraft Seafood Boxes

Both are cold-chain packs and they want opposite things. Fruit needs air moving through it; Kraft Seafood Boxes need liquid contained and cold held in, which means a liner and as few openings as possible. Using a produce carton for seafood, or the reverse, fails quickly in both directions.

Print, and what survives a cold store

Print on produce cartons is usually minimal and functional — variety, grade, count, grower code — because the box is seen by a packhouse and a retailer rather than by a shopper. Where boxes go onto a shop floor as a display, that changes, and a shelf-ready build with a tear-off front is worth specifying instead.

Inks and coatings have to tolerate condensation without lifting, which rules out some finishes that would be fine on a dry-goods carton.

Fruit packaging across a produce range

Growers and packers usually run several formats at once, and the Kraft Food Packaging range covers the trays, punnets and retail builds that go alongside a bulk carton. Standardising the footprint across them makes palletising far simpler.

What to send with your enquiry

The produce, how long it is stored and at what temperature, and the stack height. The first sets the ventilation and inner, the second and third set the board.

Recycled content, and what the cold store does to it

Produce cartons are among the most recycled packaging there is, and most are made largely from recycled fibre. The trade is that recycled liners have shorter fibres and less wet strength, which matters more here than almost anywhere because the boxes live damp.

Where a stack is high or storage is long, it is worth testing the actual grade at the actual humidity rather than trusting a dry-lab figure. The difference between a box that holds and one that slumps is often a single grade, and it only shows in the conditions the box will really face.

Standard footprints and why they matter

Produce moves on pallets through a supply chain that expects certain footprints, and a carton sized outside them wastes space on every pallet and complicates automated handling downstream. Fitting an existing pallet module is usually worth more than the few extra units a custom size would hold.

faqs.question: What are Kraft Fruit Packaging Boxes used for?
faqs.answer: Kraft Fruit Packaging Boxes are used to pack, stack, and ship fresh produce while keeping loads stable and presentation clean. faqs.question: How do I choose the right size for fruit packaging?
faqs.answer: Start with the largest fruit size in the batch and include any liners or pads you will use. The goal is controlled clearance so fruit doesn’t roll into edges or press into corners. A size that is too loose increases bruising risk, while a size that is too tight slows packing and causes pressure marks.

faqs.question: Do ventilation holes weaken the box strength?
faqs.answer: Vent holes can reduce panel strength if they are placed too close to corners or fold stress areas. A well-planned vent layout keeps airflow where it is needed while protecting edge zones that carry stack load. Testing filled stacking is the best way to confirm stability before large runs.

faqs.question: Are these boxes suitable for cold storage and chilled transit?
faqs.answer: Yes, they can be used in chilled cycles when the structure and moisture control choices match your environment. Condensation and humidity can soften paper fibers, so lined or coated options may help maintain stiffness. Carton layout and safe stack height also matter in cold rooms.

faqs.question: What helps reduce bruising during transport?
faqs.answer: Controlled fit, stable stacking, and movement control are the main factors. Liners, pads, or simple dividers can reduce rubbing and prevent fruit from rolling into corners. Matching depth to fruit size also prevents top-layer pressure from compressing lower layers.

faqs.question: What is the difference between fruit boxes and vegetable boxes?
faqs.answer: Fruit often needs gentler handling and more movement control because many fruits bruise easily. Vegetables can be heavier and denser, so wall strength and base support become higher priorities. Both need smart stacking and carton planning, but the fit strategy can differ.

faqs.question: Can I use these boxes for mixed produce shipments?
faqs.answer: Yes, mixed shipments work well when the inside layout prevents rubbing between different items. Divider grids or layer sheets help separate products and keep the kit organized. A stable footprint also improves master-carton efficiency for mixed loads.

faqs.question: What finishes are available for kraft produce packaging?
faqs.answer: Common choices include Matte, Gloss, and Spot UV, selected based on handling and visibility needs. Matte can reduce glare under warehouse lighting and keep labels readable. Gloss can strengthen contrast for branding, while Spot UV highlights selected design areas.

faqs.question: How do I keep printed labels readable after handling?

faqs.question: Are carry slots a good idea for produce boxes?
faqs.answer: Carry slots can improve grip and speed up handling on packing lines. They work best when placed away from corner stress zones and reinforced if loads are heavy. Testing filled lifting is important to confirm comfort and panel stability.

faqs.question: How do I plan safe stacking height on pallets?
faqs.answer: Safe stacking depends on filled weight per box, board strength, and how evenly fruit is layered. Start with conservative stack height and test for bulge, corner compression, and base bowing. Once you confirm stability, you can set a repeatable stacking limit for daily dispatch.

faqs.question: Do liners help in humid environments?
faqs.answer: Yes, liners can reduce moisture absorption and help panels stay firmer in damp or chilled conditions. They can also keep the inside cleaner when condensation is present. The liner choice should match your storage temperature, humidity, and handling cycle.

faqs.question: What packing routine keeps fruit centered inside the box?
faqs.answer: Use even layering and avoid overfilling so fruit stays below the edge pressure line. If needed, add pads or separators to reduce rolling. A consistent depth matched to fruit size helps keep weight distributed and reduces side pressure during transit.

description:
Kraft Gable Boxes, Built Around the Handle

A gable box is defined by one feature: the handle formed from the box itself, with no separate part to attach. That is what makes it convenient and it is also the single point of failure — everything the box carries hangs from a die-cut in folded board. At Kraft Box Pack we specify Kraft Gable Boxes from the loaded weight, because a handle that tears fails while someone is carrying it.

Whether you are sourcing kraft gable boxes wholesale for catering or a retail gift range, the first number to settle is what the box weighs when full.

Why Kraft gable boxes stand out

The handle is the weak point

Load concentrates at the top of the die-cut, and board tears from a small stress point. Reinforcing the handle area — a heavier caliper, a doubled panel, or a rounded rather than slotted cut-out — is what keeps it intact. A rounded cut is stronger than a straight slot for the same reason a rounded corner resists cracking.

The top closes but does not seal

The two gable panels fold over and lock, which is quick and secure enough for carrying and is not airtight. That suits dry and ambient items and works against anything that needs a moisture barrier, unless an inner liner or bag does that work instead.

Assembly is fast, which is the point

A gable folds up and locks in one movement, which is why the format survives in busy service environments. A design that needs several folds loses the advantage the shape was chosen for.

What actually goes in them

Gable boxes carry meals, party food, small gifts and retail sets, and the loads differ enormously. A cupcake box and a full lunch weigh nothing alike, and the same dieline will serve one and fail the other. Specifying to your heaviest realistic fill rather than the average is what avoids the failures.

Key elements of gable box design

  1. Handle rated for the heaviest fill, not the average.

  2. Rounded cut-out rather than a straight slot.

  3. Heavier caliper or a doubled panel at the handle.

  4. Liner or inner bag where a barrier is needed.

  5. One-motion assembly, since these are made up in service.

Comparison with Kraft Cake Boxes

A gable carries; a cake box presents and protects. Kraft Cake Boxes hold a decorated item flat and still, which a gable cannot do because its contents sit in a deep well and shift. Anything with icing or a topper belongs in a flat box, and the gable is for items that can tolerate being carried upright.

Print, and the shape of the panel

The front panel of a gable narrows towards the top, so artwork centred on a rectangle sits oddly. Designing to the actual trapezoid — logo low, detail in the wide part — reads far better than fitting a square design into a shape that is not square.

The handle also splits the top of the design in two. Anything crossing that line is interrupted, so it is worth treating the two gable panels as separate surfaces rather than one.

Printing and Wholesale Options for Kraft Gable Boxes

Gables usually appear alongside other formats in a range, and the Kraft Packaging Boxes collection covers the flat, tuck and mailer builds that go with them. Sharing one board and print system across the set is what makes a catering or gift range look coordinated.

What to send with your enquiry

The heaviest fill, how far it is carried, and whether anything inside needs a barrier. The first two set the handle and caliper; the third decides the liner.

Sizes, and how the shape wastes space

A gable box is tall for its footprint and its top is a peak rather than a flat surface, so it does not stack and it does not pack tightly. That costs on a pallet and it costs on a shelf, and it is the reason the format is used for carrying rather than for storing.

Flat-packed, the same box takes almost no space, which is why these are almost always delivered flat and made up as needed. Where a caterer needs a hundred assembled at once, that is an hour of someone's time to plan for rather than a surprise on the day.

Windows, and where they go

A window on a gable usually sits in the front trapezoid panel, away from the handle and away from the fold at the top. Cut too high and it weakens the panel exactly where the load pulls; cut low and it shows the contents without costing structural strength.

Kraft Gift Boxes With Lids for Secure and Elegant Packaging

A lidded box is bought for one moment — the lift — and everything about the specification serves it. At Kraft Box Pack we cut Kraft Gift Boxes With Lids so the lid comes away with a little resistance and then releases, because a lid that drops off feels cheap and one that has to be fought feels worse.

Whether you are comparing kraft gift boxes with lids wholesale or sizing a range, the number that decides it is the clearance between lid and base — small enough to feel considered, large enough to survive humidity.

Applications of kraft gift boxes with lids

Why the tolerance is the product

Board swells and shrinks with the moisture in the air. A lid cut to fit exactly in a dry factory binds in a damp warehouse, and one cut loose enough to be safe slides off in a stack. That clearance is a few tenths of a millimetre and it is set at dieline stage, not adjusted afterwards.

Two pieces, two costs

A lid and base is two dielines, two print passes and two assembly steps, so it costs meaningfully more than a tuck end. It buys reusability: this is the box a customer keeps, which is why it suits gifting and repeat-purchase ranges rather than single-use items.

Depth changes the feel

A shallow lid over a deep base reads as a presentation box. A deep lid covering most of the base reads as a shipper. The same footprint can feel like either, and it costs nothing to choose deliberately at dieline stage.

Key elements of lidded gift box design

  1. Lid clearance set at dieline stage for humidity.

  2. Lid depth chosen for how the box should read.

  3. Inserts where the contents would otherwise move.

  4. Ribbon pulls on deeper boxes, so the lid lifts cleanly.

  5. Flat-packed or pre-assembled, depending on your labour.

Options Kraft Gift Boxes With Mini Kraft Boxes

Ranges usually need more than one size, and small items in a large lidded box look lost however good the board is. Pairing the main size with Mini Kraft Boxes covers samples, add-ons and single items on the same board and print system, so a set reads as one family.

Design considerations for retail and gifting

The inside face is worth more here than on almost any other format, because a lidded box is opened deliberately and slowly. Printing the inner lid costs one extra pass and is the only part of the pack the customer looks at while their hands are still full.

Where the box will be posted, remember that the lid is the panel that takes corner crush. A separate outer protects it for a fraction of what reprinting costs.

There is a longer write-up on kraft gift boxes with lids for retail products if you are weighing the format against a tuck end.

Rigid or folding, and what separates them

A rigid box is wrapped board with a greyboard core. It holds its shape indefinitely, feels substantially heavier in the hand and cannot be flat-packed, so it costs more to make and considerably more to ship. A folding lid and base does the same job on paper, ships flat and costs a fraction, at the price of a lid that loosens with repeated use.

The question that settles it is how many times the box will be opened. A box opened once and kept for storage can be folding. A box that is part of the product — a watch box, a keepsake — earns rigid, because the twentieth opening should feel like the first.

Inserts, and when they are worth more than the box

On anything with more than one component, the insert does more for the unboxing than the outer ever will. Contents that shift in a single cavity read as an incomplete product, however good the printing is. Board inserts are the cheapest and suit light items; foam suits weight and fragility; moulded pulp sits between the two and keeps the pack in the paper stream.

description:
Kraft Gift Card Boxes, Sized to a Card

A gift card box has an unusual brief: it holds something almost weightless and almost flat, and its entire job is to make that feel like a present. At Kraft Box Pack we cut Kraft Gift Card Boxes around the card and a way of holding it, because a card sliding loose in an envelope-sized box undoes the reason for buying a box at all.

Whether you are sourcing gift card boxes wholesale for retail or a corporate programme, the decisions are how the card is held, whether there is room for a message, and how the box performs on a counter display.

Holding a card that weighs nothing

Slots, cushions and pockets

A pair of die-cut slots holds a card flat and square and costs nothing beyond the cutting forme. A foam or board cushion raises it slightly so it is the first thing seen on opening. A pocket hides it until it is pulled out. Each reads differently and all three beat a card lying loose.

Room for a message

Most gift cards are given with something written, and a box with nowhere for a note means the note goes on top of the card or not at all. A second slot, a printed panel or a small insert card solves it and is almost always worth the space.

Depth is what makes it a gift

A box only as deep as the card reads as a sleeve. A little depth, with the card raised on a cushion, reads as a presentation box. The difference in material is negligible; the difference in how it feels is not.

On a counter, in a rack

Gift card boxes usually sell from a display rather than a shelf, which means they are seen face-on and picked up repeatedly. A hang tab, a flat front panel and a finish that resists fingerprints all matter more here than on packaging that sits still until it is bought.

Key elements of gift card box design

  1. Slots, cushion or pocket, so the card is held.

  2. Space for a message, since most are given with one.

  3. Enough depth that it reads as a box, not a sleeve.

  4. A front panel designed for a rack display.

  5. A finish that resists handling marks.

Comparison with Kraft Invitation Boxes

The formats are close and the contents differ in one important way. Kraft Invitation Boxes hold printed matter that must stay perfectly flat and unmarked, often with several pieces in a set, so the fit and the rigidity matter more. A gift card box holds one small item and spends its effort on presentation instead.

Print at a small size

Fine type disappears on a small panel and uncoated kraft spreads ink slightly, so setting type larger than the design suggests is the usual fix. Foil and emboss work particularly well at this size because the whole surface is close to the eye, and they cost less than on a large box simply because there is less to cover.

Where the card itself is colourful, letting the box stay quiet gives it somewhere to sit. A busy box and a busy card compete and neither wins.

Gift cards within a wider range

Gift card boxes are almost always part of a larger collection, and the Custom Gift Boxes range covers the lidded, drawer and hamper builds they sit beside. Sharing one board and print system is what stops the smallest item in a range looking like an afterthought.

What to send with your enquiry

The card dimensions, whether a message goes with it, and whether the box hangs on a rack. Those three settle the hold, the depth and the front panel.

Volume, and why these are ordered in thousands

A gift card box is small and simple, so almost the entire cost is the cutting forme and the press run rather than the board. The unit price therefore falls steeply with quantity and then flattens, and a retailer ordering ten thousand pays a very different price per box from one ordering five hundred.

Where a range needs several designs, the cheapest route is usually one dieline with different print rather than different boxes. The tooling is paid once and the artwork carries the variation, which also makes reordering a single design simple later.

Seasonal versions without new tooling

A plain box with a printed sleeve or a seasonal label lets one production run cover a whole year. It costs a little more per unit at the point of sale and removes the risk of holding four seasonal designs, three of which are wrong by February.

description:
Kraft Gift Hamper Boxes, Built Around Mixed Contents

A hamper is the hardest gift box to specify because nothing inside it matches. Jars, bottles, packets and boxes all differ in height, weight and fragility, and left loose they migrate into each other on the first corner. At Kraft Box Pack we build Kraft Gift Hamper Boxes around the tray, because the tray is what makes a mixed set arrive looking arranged.

Whether you are sourcing hamper boxes wholesale for a seasonal range or a corporate programme, the decisions are the compartment layout, the base construction and how much weight goes in.

Why the compartment tray is the product

Everything at one level

A hamper reads well when the tops of the contents sit at roughly the same height. A tray with cells cut to different depths achieves that with items that are nothing alike, and it is the single thing that separates a designed hamper from a box of things.

Cells stop migration

Jars and bottles rolling against each other chip and can break, and even where nothing breaks the set arrives disordered. A cell per item stops it, and it is cheaper than the replacements.

Weight lands on the base

A full hamper is heavy — several kilograms is common — and it is usually lifted from underneath. A full-overlap or double-thickness base carries that; a single glued seam is where a loaded hamper fails, always at the worst moment.

Fixed contents or a flexible tray

A tray cut for one exact set is the best-looking and the least forgiving: change a supplier's jar size and the tooling is wrong. A tray with slightly generous cells and a paper wrap or shred to take up the slack costs a little in neatness and adapts across a season. Which is right depends on whether the contents are locked before the boxes are ordered.

Key elements of hamper box design

  1. A compartment tray, with cells at depths that level the tops.

  2. Full-overlap base, since a loaded hamper is heavy.

  3. Generous cells where contents may change between seasons.

  4. Handles or a ribbon on anything a customer carries.

  5. A shipping outer, because a hamper lid takes corner crush.

Comparison with Kraft Luxury Magnet Boxes

Both present a set and they suit different ones. Kraft Luxury Magnet Boxes open flat and show items of similar height laid out — cosmetics, technology, stationery. A hamper handles items of wildly different heights and weights, which a magnetic lid would struggle to close over. Choosing by the contents rather than by prestige avoids paying for the wrong build.

Seasonality, and ordering against it

Hampers are overwhelmingly seasonal, and the season is short. Lead time matters more than price, because a late delivery has nowhere to go. Ordering a plain box early and adapting it with a printed sleeve or a label is the usual way to keep flexibility without risking the date.

Hampers within a gift collection

A hamper is usually the top of a range rather than all of it, and the Custom Gift Boxes collection covers the smaller lidded, drawer and window builds beneath it. Sharing one board and print system is what makes a three-tier range read as one family.

What to send with your enquiry

The contents and their heights, the total loaded weight, and whether the hamper is carried or posted. The first sets the tray, the second the base, the third whether you need an outer.

Presentation once the lid is off

A hamper is opened slowly and looked at for longer than most packaging, so the inside is doing more work than the outside. A printed tray, a paper shred that matches the brand, or simply a printed inner lid all cost one extra pass and change what the opening feels like.

The reverse is also true: a beautifully printed outer over a plain grey tray reads as a shortcut, and the tray is the part in the photograph the recipient takes.

Sizing when the contents are not final

Hampers are frequently ordered before the contents are locked, which is a genuine risk on tooled trays. The safe approach is to fix the box size early from the largest expected item, and leave the tray until the range is confirmed — trays are quicker to tool than boxes and can be ordered later without holding up the print run.

description:
Kraft Giveaway Packaging Boxes, Handed to People Who Did Not Ask

A giveaway box goes to somebody who is already carrying a tote, a lanyard, a coffee and four other people's leaflets. Whether it survives the walk to the exit is decided in about two seconds, and almost entirely by its size and shape. At Kraft Box Pack we specify Kraft Giveaway Packaging Boxes around being carried, because a box left on a chair achieved nothing.

That is the whole difference between this and any pack a customer has chosen to receive.

What decides whether it is kept

It has to fit in the bag

Trade shows hand out a tote at the door, and anything that will not drop into it is carried by hand until the recipient tires of it. Checking your box against a standard event tote is a five-minute exercise that changes the outcome more than any design decision.

It has to be light

Weight is what people notice at the end of a day on their feet. A giveaway that is heavy for its apparent value is put down, and rigid board is exactly the wrong instinct here even though it feels generous.

It has to survive a bag

Once it goes into the tote it is crushed against everything else all afternoon. A pack that arrives home dented has failed, so the construction needs to be light and stiff rather than heavy and soft.

Key elements of giveaway box design

  1. Sized to drop into a standard event tote.

  2. Light in the hand, stiff enough to resist a crushed bag.

  3. Brand readable while it sits on a table, before it is picked up.

  4. Undated artwork, so leftovers carry to the next event.

  5. Quantity set from footfall, ordered with a margin.

Undated artwork is worth real money

Event-specific printing — a date, a stand number, a show name — turns every unsold unit into waste the moment the doors close, and the take-up rate on a giveaway is never what the forecast said. Keeping the box itself generic and putting the event detail on a card or a sticker inside means the surplus goes into the next show. Over a season that is usually a larger saving than any price negotiated on the boxes.

Quantity, and the two ways it goes wrong

Running out on the first morning is the visible failure and the more painful one, because the stand spends the rest of the show apologising. Ordering three times what is needed is the quiet failure and costs more. Footfall figures from the organiser, halved, are a more reliable basis than an internal estimate, and a margin on top is cheap when the artwork is undated and the leftovers travel.

Comparison with Kraft Event Favor Boxes

Both are made in a batch for one day and they differ in who receives them. Kraft Event Favor Boxes go to an invited guest list, so the count is known, the box sits at a place setting and nobody has to be persuaded to take it. A giveaway goes to strangers who are free to decline it, which puts the whole specification onto being wanted and being carryable.

Kraft as the message

An unbleached brown box says something about a company before anybody reads the logo, and at an event that is doing work in the two seconds before a decision is made. It reads as unfussy and as low waste. The trade is colour — bright inks shift over a brown base and pale tones vanish, so a brand built on a specific corporate colour will need a printed white base under it or a different material entirely.

Lead time against a fixed date

An event does not move. Work backwards from the day the boxes must be on a stand rather than from the show date, and allow for the proof, the print and the transport to the venue. Anything that arrives the day after the doors open is a total loss rather than a delay, which makes this the one product where the schedule deserves more attention than the specification.

Within a wider gift range

Giveaways usually sit alongside a company's customer-facing packaging, and the Custom Gift Boxes collection covers what that looks like. Building both from one board and one print treatment means somebody who meets the brand at a show recognises it when they order.

The contents, the expected footfall, and the date the boxes must be on site. We will size the box against a standard tote and work the schedule back from the date.

  • Fast turnaround times at wholesale rates

description:
Heart-Shaped Cardboard Box Design For Gifting

A heart is the hardest common shape to make in board, and understanding why explains almost everything about the format. It has two convex curves, a sharp point and a deep notch, and a notch is the one feature folded board genuinely resists — the material wants to spring back. At Customkraft Boxes we build Kraft Heart Shaped Boxes as rigid wrapped construction for that reason, because a folded heart rarely holds its curve for long.

Whether you are sourcing heart shaped boxes wholesale for a season or a single retail run, the decision that shapes both the cost and the finish is rigid or folding, and the honest answer is usually rigid.

Material choices for Paper Heart Box durability

Why rigid holds the shape

A rigid box is greyboard cut to shape and wrapped in printed paper. The board holds the curve permanently because it was cut to it rather than bent into it, and the wrap hides the join. A folding version has to score curves as a series of short creases, which reads as faceted rather than smooth, and the notch tends to open with handling.

What the wrap costs and buys

Wrapping is a hand or semi-automatic operation, which is why rigid heart boxes cost several times a folding carton of the same footprint. It buys a smooth curve, a heavier feel and a surface that takes foil and emboss well. On a seasonal gift that lands in the customer's hand once, it is usually worth it.

The point is the weak spot

The bottom point takes every knock and shows every scuff, because it protrudes. Rounding it very slightly — a few millimetres of radius, invisible in use — removes most of the damage without changing how the shape reads.

Custom sizing ideas for Heart Boxes retail use

Heart boxes waste space and it is worth planning for. They do not tessellate, so a shelf or a shipping carton holds noticeably fewer than a rectangle of the same footprint, and the freight cost per unit runs higher. Where a range ships in volume, nesting sizes so a small heart travels inside a larger carton recovers some of it.

The other sizing question is depth. A shallow heart reads as a chocolate box; a deep one reads as a keepsake. The same outline in two depths gives two quite different products from one dieline family.

Key elements of heart box design

  1. Rigid construction, so the curve and notch hold.

  2. A slight radius on the bottom point, to survive handling.

  3. Depth chosen for whether it reads as confectionery or keepsake.

  4. A fitted tray, since contents shift more in a curved cavity.

  5. Freight planned around a shape that does not tessellate.

Heart Shaped Gift Boxes with rigid kraft strength

Closure options change the format completely. A lift-off lid is the classic confectionery build. A ribbon tie suits the shape well, because the notch gives the ribbon somewhere natural to sit — which is the same reasoning behind Kraft Ribbon Closure Boxes, where the tie is the closure rather than a decoration added afterwards.

Bulk Heart Boxes planning for consistent brand sets

Heart boxes are almost entirely seasonal, and the season is short. That makes lead time the real constraint rather than price: rigid construction takes longer than folding, and a late run has nowhere to go. Ordering against the season rather than against demand is the usual approach, with a plain wrap that a sleeve or a label can adapt if the range changes.

Keepsake and jewellery Rigid, deep Lid or ribbon Matte, emboss Foam or velvet insert

Wholesale workflow for multi-SKU heart launches

Ranges usually pair the heart with rectangular formats so the whole collection can ship and merchandise sensibly, and the Custom Gift Boxes range covers those builds on the same board and print system. The heart carries the season; the rectangles carry the volume.

What to send with your enquiry

The outline width you want, the depth, and the date the range has to be on shelf. The first two set the tooling; the third matters most, because rigid construction cannot be rushed.

Printing and finishing on a curved outline

A rigid heart is printed on the wrap rather than on the box, which means the artwork is laid out flat and then formed around the shape. Anything positioned near the notch or the point distorts slightly as the paper is drawn in, so type and logos want to sit in the flatter areas — the two upper lobes take detail best.

Foil and emboss both work well here, and a metallic edge following the outline defines the curve in a way flat colour cannot.

Colour on kraft, at this scale

The wrap can be kraft or a coated paper over the same greyboard, and that choice matters more on a heart than on a rectangle. Kraft warms every colour, which suits the reds and golds the format usually carries and works against pastels. Where a pale palette is fixed, a coated white wrap over kraft board keeps the structure and the colour both.

Choose Kraft Heart Shaped Boxes built rigid so the curve survives the season. We provide:

  • Gloss, matte, and spot UV coating options

  • Free design and free shipping

  • Rigid wrapped construction with foil and emboss

  • Food-safe and eco-friendly kraft material

  • Fast turnaround times at wholesale rates

Send your outline width, depth and on-shelf date and we will plan the run backwards from it.

description:
Kraft Influencer Boxes, Designed for a Camera

Most packaging is judged after it is opened. An influencer box is judged while it is being opened, on video, by an audience — which makes the opening sequence the product and the contents almost secondary. At Kraft Box Pack we design a Kraft Influencer Box around what the camera sees in the first ten seconds.

That is a genuinely different brief. It is the only pack we make where the failure mode is being boring rather than being damaged.

What the camera actually rewards

A first look that is not cardboard

Lift the lid on a plain box and the shot is brown board and a bag of filler. Inside printing, a tissue layer or a printed tray changes that moment completely, and it is the cheapest upgrade available on this product because it needs no structural change at all.

An opening with one clear action

A magnetic closure, a ribbon pull or a clean tear strip gives the video a single decisive movement. A box that has to be wrestled open, or cut, breaks the shot and the person filming will edit it out — along with your branding.

Items revealed rather than found

A fitted tray presents everything at once and in an order you chose. Loose items in filler have to be dug out one at a time, which looks like a delivery rather than a gift.

Key elements of influencer box design

  1. Inside print or a lined interior, since that is the first frame.

  2. One decisive opening action, with no knife required.

  3. A fitted tray that reveals the contents in a chosen order.

  4. A hand-written or personalised card, which is what gets shown.

  5. An outer shipper, so the box itself arrives unmarked.

The mistake that ruins the shot

These boxes are usually posted, and a beautifully finished box sent as its own shipper arrives scuffed, labelled and stamped. Everything spent on the finish is then hidden under a courier sticker in exactly the frame it was bought for. An outer carton costs a fraction of the box it protects, and sending the presentation box inside a plain shipper is the difference between the video starting with your brand and starting with a delivery bag.

Personalisation at small volumes

Campaigns run in dozens rather than thousands, which changes the economics in a useful direction. At fifty units a printed card, a name on a sleeve or a variable insert is realistic in a way it never is on a retail line, and the personal element is reliably the part that gets shown on camera. It is worth spending there rather than on a more elaborate box.

Comparison with Kraft Marketing Kit Boxes

The two are close relatives with different audiences. Kraft Marketing Kit Boxes go to a buyer or a journalist and are built to carry information — samples, a spec sheet, something that will be filed. An influencer box goes to a camera and is built to be watched, so the budget moves from the printed material inside to the reveal itself.

Weight, and what it signals

A heavy box feels considered before anything is opened, and on camera that registers as production value. Rigid board delivers it and costs both money and postage; a corrugated mailer with a well-made tray gets most of the way there for far less. Campaign boxes usually borrow from a brand's existing gift packaging rather than starting fresh, and the Custom Gift Boxes collection covers what that range holds. Using the same board and print treatment means a campaign send and a customer order look like the same company.

description:
Kraft Insulated Cold Boxes, Specified in Hours

Insulation does not make anything cold. It slows the rate at which the cold you packed leaks away, which means the specification is a duration rather than a temperature. At Kraft Box Pack the first question on a Kraft Insulated Cold Box is how many hours it has to hold, measured from the moment it is sealed to the moment somebody opens it.

That number is longer than most people first say. A parcel posted on Friday afternoon is a weekend, not an overnight.

The four things that set the hours

Coolant mass

Gel packs and dry ice are the actual cold. Doubling the insulation buys far less time than adding a second gel pack, and the coolant is usually the cheaper adjustment.

Liner thickness

Performance scales with thickness, and thickness eats internal volume. Every extra millimetre of liner is a millimetre off the product space inside the same outer, which is why the outer and the payload have to be sized together.

Headspace

Air is the enemy. A half-full insulated box performs noticeably worse than a full one, because the air circulates and carries heat to the contents. Filling the void with more coolant or with packing is not optional padding — it is part of the thermal specification.

Ambient at the far end

A box that holds for twenty-four hours in a cool warehouse may hold for twelve on a doorstep in August. Design to the destination and the season, not to the test bench.

Condensation, and what it does to board

Cold inside and warm outside puts water somewhere, and on a paper-based pack that matters. If the moisture reaches the kraft outer, the board softens and loses stiffness exactly when it is carrying a heavy load of coolant. The liner has to hold the water on its own inside face, and the outer usually wants a moisture-resistant coating as well. This is the failure people do not anticipate, and it shows up as a collapsed base rather than a warm product.

Key elements of cold box design

  1. A hold time set from the worst realistic journey, including weekends.

  2. Coolant mass calculated before liner thickness is increased.

  3. Headspace filled, since air circulates and carries heat.

  4. A moisture-resistant outer, because condensation lands on the board.

  5. A vent where dry ice is used, since it must be allowed to gas off.

The liner decides the disposal claim

Expanded polystyrene performs well per millimetre and makes the pack a mixed material that no household can put out for collection. Recycled fibre and wool liners are kerbside-recyclable or compostable and need more thickness for the same hours. There is no free answer here, only a choice about which constraint matters more to the brand — and whichever is chosen, the disposal instruction printed on the box has to describe the liner that was actually bought.

Comparison with Kraft Thermal Kraft Boxes

The two overlap and are not the same job. Kraft Thermal Kraft Boxes hold a temperature over a short, known journey — a delivery across a city, an hour at most — so a modest liner and no coolant is often enough. A cold box is built for a multi-day chain with an active coolant load inside it, which changes the board, the closure and the weight.

Use Hold time Coolant Liner Notes
Meal kits 24-48 hours Gel packs Fibre Headspace varies weekly
Fresh meat and fish 24-48 hours Gel packs Fibre or wool Leak containment required
Frozen goods 48 hours plus Dry ice High density Must vent, must be labelled
Pharmaceuticals Validated Phase change High density Needs documented testing
Chilled retail transfer 6-12 hours Gel packs Fibre Reused between sites
Flowers and plants 12-24 hours None Thin fibre Cool, not cold, is the target

Weight is the hidden cost

Gel packs are water, and water is heavy. A pack with two litres of coolant carries two kilograms before the product goes in, which pushes the parcel into a higher carrier band and loads the base of the box far more than the contents suggest. A full-overlap base is not a luxury on a cold box, and the freight on the coolant is worth checking before the hold time is fixed generously.

Within an industrial range

Cold chain packaging rarely stands alone, and the Kraft Industrial Packaging collection covers the outer cartons, transit boxes and heavy-duty formats around it. Running one board specification across a site keeps the handling and the storage consistent.

What to send with your enquiry

The hold time in hours, the payload volume and weight, and the coolant you intend to use. From those we can size the outer and the liner together rather than one after the other.

faqs.question: What is the difference between kraft cold storage boxes and standard kraft boxes?
faqs.answer: Kraft cold storage boxes are planned with space for cooling elements and a more controlled inner fit. Standard kraft boxes are usually built for dry products without gel packs, liners, or condensation control. Cold storage versions focus more on stable placement, insulation spacing, and packing repeatability.

faqs.question: What are kraft insulated chiller boxes best suited for?
faqs.answer: Kraft insulated chiller boxes are best suited for deliveries where products need to stay cool for a limited time, such as local shipping, same-day delivery, or short courier routes. They are also used when a brand wants a neat unboxing layout that still supports chill protection. Inserts can be added to keep multi-item kits organized.

faqs.question: Can I order Kraft insulated cold boxes wholesale?
faqs.answer: Yes, these are commonly ordered in bulk when brands run recurring chilled programs or campaigns. Wholesale ordering works best when size, depth, insert layout, and finish settings are finalized early. This keeps reorders consistent and reduces packing variability across batches.

faqs.question: What products can be shipped in insulated kraft boxes for cold items?
faqs.answer: These boxes are used for chilled desserts, dairy-based items, meal kits, beverages in sealed packs, skincare products that benefit from cool transit, and sample kits with temperature sensitivity. The key is planning the insert layout and gel pack placement so items remain centered. Product protection and presentation can be balanced in one system.

faqs.question: How should gel packs be placed inside the box?
faqs.answer: Gel packs should be placed in planned pockets or along side channels so they stay near the product surfaces without pressing too hard. The layout should avoid direct contact with paper cards or booklets where condensation can cause damage. Inserts help prevent gel packs from drifting during transit movement.

faqs.question: How do I prevent items from shifting inside kraft refrigerated packaging boxes?
faqs.answer: Use inserts, divider grids, or foam supports that hold items in fixed positions. A close-fit layout reduces empty space and limits sliding. When items stay centered, gel pack placement remains effective and the unboxing presentation stays neat.

faqs.question: What sizes are available for kraft thermal cold boxes?
faqs.answer: Sizes are typically customized based on product dimensions and the cooling system you plan to use. A good size includes controlled clearance for inserts and gel packs without creating unnecessary void space. Many programs keep a standard footprint and adjust depth for different kit variants.

faqs.question: Do these boxes help with packaging boxes wholesale programs for cold items?
faqs.answer: Yes, because they support repeatable packing routines and consistent presentation across large runs. When dielines and insert layouts are standardized, staff can pack faster and kits arrive in better condition. This consistency is often the main goal in bulk cold shipment programs.

faqs.question: Which finishes work best for refrigerated shipping conditions?
faqs.answer: Matte finishes reduce glare and can hide minor rub marks under normal lighting. Gloss finishes add shine and can make printed areas appear stronger, while Spot UV highlights selected logo zones without changing the full surface. Finish choice should match handling frequency and transit exposure.

faqs.question: Can printing stay readable on kraft surfaces for cold box branding?
faqs.answer: Yes, if contrast and spacing are planned carefully. Lid and front panels are usually treated as primary branding areas because they show in photos and stacked displays. Some designs use a controlled underlayer when brighter colors are needed on kraft tones.

faqs.question: How can condensation be managed in cold shipments?
faqs.answer: Condensation can be managed by separating paper inserts from gel pack zones and using liners or moisture barrier layers where needed. Keeping items centered also reduces movement that can spread moisture. A planned layout is the simplest way to reduce condensation-related presentation issues.

faqs.question: Are kraft insulated cold boxes suitable for influencer and PR cold drops?
faqs.answer: Yes, because they can deliver a neat unboxing layout while still supporting chill protection. A structured inside view helps when recipients film or photograph the unboxing. Inserts and print planning keep the presentation consistent even after transit handling.

faqs.question: What details should I share before producing a bulk order?
faqs.answer: Share product dimensions, target transit time, whether gel packs will be used, insert needs, print files, and finish preferences. Also share how units will be packed into master cartons, because carton layout affects corner rub and stacking stability. These details help ensure the box fits your real cold shipping workflow.

description:
Kraft Invitation Boxes, and the Depth That Creeps

An invitation box is specified against a stack that is not finished yet. The card is chosen, then an RSVP is added, then a details card, then vellum, then a ribbon and a wax seal — and each of those is a fraction of a millimetre that nobody counted. At Kraft Box Pack we size Kraft Invitation Boxes from a finished, assembled suite rather than from the invitation.

A box that will not close over the final stack is the most common failure on this product, and it happens weeks after the size was agreed.

Flat is the whole job

Card warps when it is loose

Paper takes moisture from the air and releases it unevenly, and a card sitting loose in an oversized tray curls at the corners within days. A snug interior holds the stack flat by contact alone, which is why an invitation box wants to be tight rather than generous.

A ribbon does structural work

A ribbon under the stack is usually there to lift the cards out, but it also holds them together as one block. That block resists warping far better than loose cards do, and it is worth designing in rather than adding as decoration.

Depth is the only forgiving dimension

Length and width are fixed by the card. Depth is the one you can adjust, and it is the one that runs out. Specify it with a few millimetres of headroom and the suite can grow without a new die.

Postage is decided by thickness

Invitations are posted, and a rigid item is charged differently from a letter. The band is usually set by thickness, so a box a couple of millimetres over a threshold moves a hundred and fifty invitations into a more expensive class at once. Measuring the sealed pack against the postal dimensions before the depth is fixed is the single most valuable half hour on this product, because at that quantity the difference is often larger than the boxes cost.

Key elements of invitation box design

  1. Sized from the finished suite, with the seal and ribbon on it.

  2. A snug interior, since a loose card warps.

  3. A pull ribbon that also holds the stack as one block.

  4. Thickness checked against the postal band before the die is cut.

  5. A few millimetres of depth in hand for what gets added later.

Kraft under printing and foil

Uncoated kraft is a warm brown with a visible fibre, and it takes some treatments better than others. Foil sits beautifully on it and is the usual choice for a monogram or a date. Fine black type holds well; fine white type does not, because there is no opaque base under it and the brown shows through. Where a design needs white detail, a printed white flood in that area first is what makes it read, and it should be specified rather than assumed.

Comparison with Kraft Round Gift Containers

Both are presentation packs and they hold opposite geometries. Kraft Round Gift Containers hold volume, ship assembled and give up the flat printable face entirely. An invitation box holds almost no volume, ships flat, and is nearly all printable face — which is why the print specification carries the product here and the construction carries it there.

Use Format Interior Finish Notes
Wedding suites Lid and base Ribbon pull Foil Depth creeps as items are added
Posted invitations Shallow tray Snug fit Print only Thickness sets the postage band
Corporate events Tuck end Card seat Print only Highest counts, plainest build
Hand-delivered VIP Rigid Fitted tray Foil and emboss Weight is part of the impression
Save the date Shallow tray Snug fit Print only Thin enough for letter rate
Suites with wax seals Lid and base Recessed seat Foil Seal needs its own clearance

Wax seals need their own space

A wax seal stands proud of the card by two or three millimetres and it is brittle. Stacked flat against a lid it cracks, and a cracked seal reads as damage rather than as character. Either the interior gives it a recess or the seal goes on the outermost item where nothing presses on it, and that has to be decided before the tray is cut.

Ordering to a fixed date

Invitations have a real deadline, and the timeline runs backwards from the day the cards must be in the post — not from the wedding. Allow for the proof, the print, and the time it takes somebody to assemble the suites by hand, which is usually longer than anyone plans for. Order a margin over the guest list at the outset, because a small second run is disproportionately expensive and may not arrive.

Within a wider event range

An invitation is normally the first of several packs for the same event, and the Custom Gift Boxes collection covers what follows it. Fixing the kraft stock and the foil at the invitation stage means everything after it matches without another decision.

What to send with your enquiry

The finished suite, measured as a stack, and the date the invitations must be posted. We will size the tray from the first and work the schedule back from the second.

  • Foil, embossing and recessed wax-seal trays

  • Food-safe and eco-friendly kraft material

  • Fast turnaround times at wholesale rates

Send the measured thickness of a finished suite and your posting date.
