description:
Kraft Paper Gift Wrapping, and What Weight to Buy

Wrapping paper has one job that decides everything about it: it has to fold sharply at a corner without splitting and without springing back. That is a property of weight and fibre rather than of print, and it is why cheap wrap tears at the corner and good wrap holds a crease. At Kraft Box Pack we supply Kraft Paper Gift Wrapping in the weights that actually behave.

Whether you are sourcing kraft wrapping paper wholesale in rolls or sheets, the number to fix first is the weight, because it governs both the fold and the cost.

Weight, and what each range does

Under 80 gsm

Light enough for void fill, shred and loose stuffing, and too light to wrap anything with an edge. It creases well and tears just as easily.

80 to 120 gsm

The working range for gift wrap. Heavy enough to hold a corner and light enough to fold twice without bulking at the join. Most retail wrapping paper sits here.

120 gsm and above

Stiff enough that a tight corner starts to resist and a double fold becomes bulky. It suits sleeves, tags and wraps around a flat product rather than parcel wrapping.

Rolls or sheets, and who is doing the wrapping

A roll is cheaper per square metre and needs cutting, which is fine at a counter with a dispenser and awkward on a busy day. Pre-cut sheets cost more and remove the step entirely. Where staff wrap during a rush, sheets sized to the commonest product usually pay for themselves in speed alone.

Key elements of specifying wrapping paper

  1. Weight in the 80 to 120 gsm range for actual wrapping.

  2. Dyed through where torn or cut edges will show.

  3. Sheets rather than rolls where speed matters at the counter.

  4. Print method matched to the run length.

  5. Ink that does not crack along a hard fold.

Comparison with Kraft Paper Packaging

Wrapping is the least protective member of the family. Kraft Paper Packaging covers the boxes, sleeves and bags that do structural work; a wrap does none, and that is precisely why it is the cheapest way to put a brand on something and the wrong answer for anything crushable.

Print, and the fold

Ink sits on the surface of uncoated paper and a hard crease can crack a heavy ink lay, which shows as a white line exactly on the corner the eye goes to. Lighter coverage, a pattern rather than a solid flood, and a water-based ink all reduce it.

A repeating pattern also hides the joins and the offcuts, which is why so much wrapping paper is patterned rather than carrying a single mark — it is a practical decision as much as a decorative one.

Use Weight Format Print Notes
Counter gift wrapping 80-120 gsm Sheets Pattern Speed at the counter
High-volume wrapping 80-120 gsm Roll Pattern Cheapest per square metre
Void fill and shred Under 80 gsm Roll Plain or dyed Dyed edges stay in colour
Sleeves and bands 120-180 gsm Sheets Any Holds a crease firmly
Tags and cards 200 gsm and up Sheets Any Behaves as board
Short runs 80-120 gsm Sheets Digital No plate cost

Wrapping within a gift range

Wrap is one layer of a set that usually includes tags, ribbon, tissue and boxes, and the Kraft Wrapping & Accessories collection covers all of them on the same stocks. Ordering them together is what stops three slightly different browns arriving from three suppliers.

What to send with your enquiry

What is being wrapped and roughly how often, whether staff cut at the counter, and your run length. The first sets the weight, the second sheets or roll, the third the print method.

Dyed through, or printed on the surface

Coloured wrapping paper comes two ways and they behave differently. Dyed in the pulp, the colour goes all the way through the fibre, so a torn or cut edge shows the same shade as the face. Printed on brown kraft, only the surface is coloured and every cut edge stays brown.

For wrapping that matters more than it sounds, because a wrap is full of folded and cut edges. Where the paper is torn deliberately as part of a look, dyed stock is the only version that survives it.

Matching across a set

Kraft varies slightly in shade between production batches, and a wrap bought in spring next to tissue bought in autumn can be visibly different. Ordering the paper for a whole gift set in one batch removes it, and is far easier than trying to match afterwards.

Storage and handling

Rolls keep well and take little room; sheets take more space and stay flat, which matters if they are printed and the crease would show. Where sheets are stored on a shelf under other stock, a wrap can arrive at the counter already marked.

  • Rolls and pre-cut sheets, quoted side by side

  • Food-safe and eco-friendly kraft material

  • Fast turnaround times at wholesale rates

Send what you wrap most often and we will size the sheets to it.

description:
Kraft Paper Packaging Across the Whole Range

Kraft is one material doing several different jobs, and the formats it takes are more varied than the boxes suggest — cartons, sleeves, wraps, bags, tubes, tags and void fill all come from the same pulp. At Kraft Box Pack we supply Kraft Paper Packaging across that whole family, and choosing between the formats is usually a more useful conversation than choosing a box size.

Whether you are sourcing kraft paper packaging wholesale or replacing a plastic component, the question worth asking first is what the packaging has to do: protect, present, carry, or simply hold something together.

Formats, and what each is actually for

Where a sleeve beats a box

A sleeve uses roughly a third of the board of a carton and carries the same print. Where the product holds its own shape — a bar, a candle, a folded garment — a sleeve does the branding job at a fraction of the cost and the shipping volume. It protects almost nothing, which is the trade.

Where a wrap beats both

Printed paper wrapped around a product costs less again and adapts to any size, which is why bakeries and delis use it for items that change shape daily. It is the cheapest way to put a brand on something and the least protective.

Where only a box will do

Anything crushable, anything stacked, anything that has to stand on a shelf unsupported. Paying for a box when a sleeve would have done is the most common overspend in this category, and using a sleeve where a box was needed is the most common damage claim.

Replacing plastic, and where kraft genuinely can

Kraft replaces plastic well for carrying, wrapping and cushioning — paper void fill, honeycomb wrap and paper tape all work as well as their plastic equivalents. It replaces plastic badly where a barrier is the whole point: a paper bag will not hold a liquid, and a coating good enough to do so usually stops the pack being recyclable, which was the reason for the change.

Key elements of specifying kraft packaging

  1. Format chosen by the job, not by habit.

  2. Sleeve or wrap where the product holds its own shape.

  3. Box where anything is crushable or stacked.

  4. Barrier claims checked against the recyclability claim.

  5. One board and print system across all the formats used.

Comparison with Kraft Paper Dispenser Boxes

Some formats exist for how the packaging is emptied rather than how it is filled. Kraft Paper Dispenser Boxes are built around a perforation that has to tear cleanly and leave an opening that holds its shape as the contents come out — a demand no ordinary carton faces, and one that changes the board specification.

Keeping a range coherent

Most businesses end up using four or five kraft formats, bought at different times from different suppliers, and it shows: three slightly different browns and two print styles across one counter. Specifying the whole family from one board at the outset costs nothing extra and is very difficult to retrofit.

Printed Kraft Paper Packaging for Retail

The wraps, tags, sleeves and bags that go around a box are covered in the Kraft Wrapping & Accessories range, on the same stocks as the cartons. That is what lets a small brand look like it planned its packaging rather than accumulated it.

What to send with your enquiry

What the product is, whether it holds its own shape, and whether it is stacked or posted. Those three usually decide the format before any conversation about size.

Ordering across formats at once

Buying a box in March, a sleeve in July and bags in October means three setups, three minimum quantities and three chances for the brown to differ. Specifying the whole family in one enquiry usually prices better than the sum of the parts, because the board is bought once and the artwork is prepared once.

It also fixes the shade problem before it happens. Kraft drifts slightly between production batches, and a counter holding three different browns looks accidental in a way no single item does.

Minimums, per format

Minimums differ by format rather than by supplier preference. Wraps and sleeves come from a sheet and have low minimums; anything requiring a cutting forme carries the tooling cost until the quantity absorbs it. That is worth knowing when a range includes one high-volume item and several small ones.

  • Free design and free shipping

  • Cartons, sleeves, wraps and bags on one board

  • Food-safe and eco-friendly kraft material

  • Fast turnaround times at wholesale rates

description:
Kraft Paper Treat Bags, Which Have No Shape of Their Own

A bag is not a small box. It has no fixed volume, no rigid wall and no ability to protect anything — it takes whatever shape the contents give it, and everything that is good and bad about the format follows from that. At Kraft Box Pack we specify Kraft Paper Treat Bags for how they are filled and carried rather than for what they hold.

Which is why the base construction is the decision that matters, and almost the only one.

The base decides everything

Flat bottom bags stand up

A square-cut gusseted base lets the bag stand open on a counter, which means one person can fill it with one hand and a scoop. On a busy counter that is the difference between serving quickly and needing two hands for every order.

Pinch bottom bags do not

Cheaper, flatter to store, and they need holding open while they are filled. Fine where bags are packed in advance in a back room, awkward where they are filled to order in front of a customer.

Gussets set the real capacity

The printed dimensions of a bag describe it flat. Loaded, the side gussets open and the usable volume is quite different from what the flat measurement suggests, which is why bags are best chosen against a filled sample rather than from a size chart.

Key elements of treat bag design

  1. A flat base wherever bags are filled to order at a counter.

  2. A grease-resistant liner for anything buttery or warm.

  3. Artwork placed on the flat front, clear of the gusset folds.

  4. A closure chosen from how long the bag has to stay shut.

  5. Capacity confirmed with a filled sample, not a flat size.

Grease is the recurring problem

Warm biscuits, pastries and anything fried will mark plain kraft within minutes, and a translucent patch spreading across a printed front is the fastest way to make fresh food look old. A greaseproof liner or a barrier-treated paper stops it. This is a decision made when the paper is chosen, not something a coating adds later, and it is the most common thing a bakery gets wrong on its first order.

Printing on a surface that folds

A bag is printed flat and then used three-dimensionally, so the gussets fold the artwork inward and take a strip out of the design on each side. Anything that has to be read — a name, a web address — belongs in the middle of the front panel. Designs that run edge to edge look excellent flat and lose a slice of themselves the moment the bag is opened, which surprises people every time.

Comparison with Kraft Cookie Boxes

The two carry the same food and offer opposite protection. Kraft Cookie Boxes hold their shape, stack, and stop the contents being crushed, which matters for anything decorated or fragile. A bag protects nothing and wins on speed, cost and the fact that it folds flat until the second it is needed.

Use Base Barrier Closure Notes
Bakery counters Flat bottom Greaseproof Fold over Filled one handed
Sweets and pick and mix Flat bottom None Sticker Weighed at the counter
Party favours Flat bottom None Ribbon Packed in advance
Coffee beans Flat bottom Foil lined Tin tie Needs a degassing valve
Pastries to go Pinch bottom Greaseproof Fold over Fastest and cheapest
Retail pre-packed Flat bottom As needed Heat seal Stands on a shelf

Closures, and how long they have to hold

A fold-over top holds for the walk to a table. A sticker holds for the journey home. A tin tie or a heat seal holds for a shelf life. Choosing one is really choosing how long the contents have to stay in, and paying for more than that is waste — most treat bags are opened within the hour and a simple fold is genuinely sufficient.

Storage and stock

Bags take almost no space and keep indefinitely if they stay dry, which makes them one of the few packaging lines where ordering well ahead is straightforwardly cheaper. Damp is the one enemy: paper that has taken on moisture in a cellar tears at the gusset and prints poorly on any later run.

Within a wider packaging range

Most counters need bags and boxes together rather than one or the other, and the Kraft Packaging Boxes collection covers the rigid formats alongside. Running one kraft shade and one logo treatment across both is what makes a takeaway counter look considered.

What to send with your enquiry

What goes in, how many bags a day, and whether they are filled to order or in advance. The last question is the one that chooses the base.

description:
Kraft Paperboard Boxes, and What Caliper Buys

Paperboard is the single-layer material that most retail packaging is made from — no fluting, no corrugation, just board of a given thickness. Everything it can do follows from that thickness, which is measured as caliper and quoted separately from weight. At Kraft Box Pack we cut Kraft Paperboard Boxes across the grades, and choosing the right one is mostly a question of unsupported panel span.

Whether you are sourcing paperboard boxes wholesale or specifying a first range, the numbers that matter are the largest flat panel and the weight it has to hold.

Why span matters more than weight

Long panels bow

A small box holds its shape at a light caliper because no panel is long enough to flex. Double the dimensions and the same board bows visibly. That is why caliper is chosen from the panel span rather than from the contents, and why small boxes can be far lighter than people expect.

Weight and caliper are not the same

Two boards at the same weight per square metre can differ in thickness, because one is bulkier. A bulkier board feels more substantial in the hand for the same money, which is a genuine lever where a box has to feel premium without costing more.

Where paperboard stops

Above a certain size and weight the answer is corrugated rather than heavier paperboard. Adding caliper past that point costs more than the fluted alternative and still performs worse in a stack.

Creasing, and why boxes crack

Board is creased before folding, and a crease that is too shallow cracks the printed surface along the fold. Heavier calipers need deeper creases, and a coated or laminated surface cracks more readily than an uncoated one. It is the most common visible fault on a finished box and it is set on the cutting forme rather than at the press.

Key elements of paperboard box design

  1. Caliper chosen from the longest unsupported panel.

  2. Bulk considered as well as weight, for how it feels.

  3. Crease depth matched to the caliper and the finish.

  4. Corrugated instead, once the span or load is too great.

  5. Grain direction set so panels fold the easy way.

Comparison with Kraft Dispenser Boxes

Structure puts different demands on the same board. Kraft Dispenser Boxes have to tear cleanly along a perforation and then stand up with part of a panel missing, which needs a board that is neither too stiff nor too soft. An ordinary carton never faces that, and a grade perfect for one can be wrong for the other.

Grain, the property nobody asks about

Board has a grain direction from the way it was made, and it folds cleanly along the grain and reluctantly across it. A dieline laid out without regard to grain gives boxes that crack on two of their four folds. It costs nothing to get right and is invisible on a drawing, which is why it is usually discovered on a sample.

Box Caliper Why Finish Notes
Small cartons Light Short panel spans Uncoated Cheaper and feels fine
Medium retail Medium Panels start to bow Matte or coated Most common grade
Large flat panels Heavy Long unsupported spans Matte Deeper creases needed
Premium feel Bulky at same weight Feels heavier in hand Uncoated Same cost, better feel
Stacked or heavy Move to corrugated Paperboard runs out Any Cheaper than more caliper
Laminated surfaces Any - Deeper crease Coatings crack more

Paperboard across a range

Most ranges use paperboard for the retail packs and something else for shipping, and the Kraft Packaging Boxes collection covers both alongside each other. Specifying them together at the start means the retail box and the outer are designed as a pair rather than bought separately and hoped to fit.

What to send with your enquiry

The largest panel dimension, the contents weight, and whether the box will be laminated. The first two set the caliper, the third sets the crease.

Coated, uncoated, and what each does to print

An uncoated board absorbs ink, which softens fine detail slightly and warms every colour. A clay-coated one holds the ink on the surface, giving sharper print and denser blacks at the cost of the natural texture that made kraft worth choosing.

Neither is better in the abstract. Photographic artwork and precise brand colours want a coating; a design built on foil, emboss and type reads better uncoated, and takes an impression that a coated surface flattens.

Recycled content and how it prints

Recycled paperboard is darker and more flecked, and the flecks show through light print. On a design using pale colours over large areas that is visible; on a dark or type-led design it is invisible and the board costs less. Deciding which your artwork can carry is worth doing before the stock is chosen rather than after a proof.

  • Gloss, matte, and spot UV coating options

  • Free design and free shipping

  • Caliper and bulk options quoted side by side

  • Food-safe and eco-friendly kraft material

  • Fast turnaround times at wholesale rates

Send your largest panel and contents weight and we will pick the caliper from both.

description:
Kraft Pastry Boxes For Fresh Counter Displays

Kraft pastry boxes help bakeries keep slices, donuts, cupcakes, and filled pastries steady from the counter to the customer’s hands, while still looking clean in photos and storefront lighting. Many teams also use Kraft Chocolate Packaging Boxes when they pack mixed dessert sets and want the same kraft tone across different items. A well-sized pastry box reduces shifting, keeps toppings from smearing the lid, and supports quick packing during rush hours without forcing the product into tight corners. When customers open the box, the first view stays neat because the product sits centered instead of sliding to one side.

Kraft pastry boxes for sale are usually evaluated by how they hold shape during stacking and how consistently the lid closes after handling. If the box walls soften, corners can round off and the lid can sit unevenly, which makes a display row look messy. For daily bakery use, the practical goal is simple: keep pastries protected, keep the box presentable, and keep packing steps fast. When you plan Kraft pastry boxes sizes properly, you also reduce wasted space, which improves carton layout and lowers movement during short delivery routes.

What Sizes Keep Pastries Stable During Transit Trips

Kraft pastry boxes sizes work best when the box matches the pastry footprint with a small, controlled clearance that allows easy placement without giving the product room to slide. For most bakeries, the best sizing method is measuring the item with its liner, tray, or parchment included, then adding minimal extra space for quick packing. This keeps icing, crumbs, and fillings from touching the lid, and it helps maintain the pastry shape when the box is carried, stacked, or placed in a delivery bag.

A second sizing detail is height, because tall toppings and delicate swirls need headroom, while flatter pastries need less depth to stay centered. If you sell mixed items, you can keep one footprint and adjust depth for different product types, which keeps your shelf look consistent. When boxes stack evenly, they handle busy counter workflows better, and they also travel more smoothly in cartons because units stay aligned instead of tilting into each other.

What Buyers Notice In Daily Bakery Handling

  • Walls stay firm so stacks do not lean during rush hours
  • Lid sits evenly so rows look tidy on the display counter

description:
Kraft Pencil Packaging Boxes, and the Break You Cannot See

Drop a boxed set of pencils and the wood will be fine. The graphite or pigment core inside may not be — it fractures in several places along its length, invisibly, and the customer discovers it later when the point breaks off at every sharpening. At Kraft Box Pack we specify Kraft Pencil Packaging Boxes around that hidden failure, because it is the one that generates complaints about the pencil rather than the box.

Coloured pencils and pastels are worse than graphite, and the softer the core the less of a drop it takes.

Stopping the shock along the length

Loose pencils hit the ends

Pencils in an open box slide the full internal length and strike the end wall together. That concentrated impact is exactly what cracks a core, and it happens on an ordinary journey rather than a rough one.

Slotted trays absorb it

A tray that seats each pencil individually stops the sliding and spreads any impact along the whole pencil rather than into its tip. On a set of any value it is the component that decides the return rate.

Pencils roll, so the box tips

Round pencils loose in a box shift the weight to one side, and a display box on a shelf ends up leaning. Flats, slots or a tray solve it at the same time as the impact problem.

Key elements of pencil box design

  1. A slotted tray, since a loose set fractures its own cores.

  2. Internal length matched to the pencil, with no room to slide.

  3. The count and grades legible, because that is the product.

  4. A lid that survives daily reopening for years.

  5. A stiff outer for anything posted, since long parcels bend.

The count is the product

Nobody buys a pencil box; they buy twelve, twenty-four or forty-eight, in stated grades or colours. The number and the range are the entire proposition, which is why a pencil pack's front panel is mostly a specification and why an accurate colour representation matters so much. A set whose printed swatches do not match the pencils inside is a set that gets returned, and on a brown kraft base that mismatch is easy to create accidentally.

A pack that stays in use for years

A pencil box sits on a desk and is opened every day it is used, which is nothing like the life of a retail carton. A tuck flap tears within a term of school use; a hinged lid or a firm friction fit keeps working. Once the lid stops closing, the pencils are stored loose in a bag and start breaking again, so the closure is protecting the product long after the sale.

Comparison with Kraft Notebook Packaging

Both are stationery packs and their failure modes are opposite. Kraft Notebook Packaging protects a flat item whose enemies are bent corners and scuffed covers, so the pack is a sleeve or a snug wrap and impact hardly matters. A pencil set is a collection of long brittle items where the whole risk is a shock travelling down the length, which is a tray problem rather than a surface one.

Use Format Interior Closure Notes
Graphite sets Tuck end Slotted tray Tuck Hardest cores, most forgiving
Coloured pencils Lid and base Slotted tray Hinged Swatch accuracy sells it
Artist grade sets Rigid Tiered tray Hinged Kept and refilled for years
School and bulk packs Tuck end None Tuck Cost led, breakage accepted
Promotional singles Sleeve None None Branding is the whole point
Gift sets Rigid Tiered tray Hinged Opened in front of someone

Tiered trays on larger sets

Above about twenty-four pencils a single layer becomes an awkward, wide box. A tiered tray that lifts to reveal a second row keeps the footprint sensible and gives a large set a moment when it is opened, which on a gift purchase is worth more than the tray costs. It also keeps the two layers from pressing on each other, which a simple double-stacked box does not.

Posting a long thin parcel

Long narrow parcels attract bending, and a pencil box that arrives with a kink has almost certainly damaged the cores inside even where the box looks recoverable. Where sets sell online, the outer needs stiffness along its length rather than padding around it, and it is worth using a slightly larger, more rigid outer than the box strictly needs.

Within an accessories range

Stationery ranges extend quickly into cases, notebooks and desk items, and the Kraft Electronics Boxes collection covers many of the formats those need. One board and one print system across them keeps a growing catalogue coherent.

What to send with your enquiry

The pencil length and diameter, the counts you want to sell, and whether the sets are posted. The counts set the trays and the postal question sets the outer.

description:
Kraft Pillow Boxes, Held by the Die-Cut

A pillow box has no glue and no lid. It is a single piece of board with curved end flaps that hold each other closed by tension, which is why it ships perfectly flat and pops into shape in one motion. At Kraft Box Pack we cut Kraft Pillow Boxes so that tension is right — too weak and the ends gape, too strong and the board creases when it is closed.

Whether you are sourcing pillow boxes wholesale for favours or a retail range, the thing to understand is that the curve is doing all the work.

What the shape can and cannot hold

Light and flat suits it

Scarves, jewellery, socks, cards, small cosmetics and confectionery all sit well in a pillow box because they do not push against the curve. The format is at its best where the contents are soft or thin.

Weight defeats it

Anything heavy pulls the curved ends open, because nothing is holding them but the board's own springiness. There is no reinforcement to add — a heavier caliper resists a little longer and then creases instead. Where the contents have real weight, the answer is a different format rather than a stronger pillow box.

The curve wastes space

The interior is lens-shaped rather than rectangular, so the usable volume is noticeably less than the outside dimensions suggest. A product that measures as a fit on paper can be too deep at the ends, which is worth checking with a sample rather than a calculation.

Why it costs so little

One dieline, one piece, no gluing, no assembly beyond a single fold. That makes pillow boxes among the cheapest formats to produce and to ship, and it is why they dominate event favours and promotional runs where quantity matters more than protection.

Key elements of pillow box design

  1. Curve tension set so ends close without creasing.

  2. Contents light and preferably flat.

  3. Interior depth checked with a sample, not a calculation.

  4. Ribbon or a sticker seal where the ends must stay shut.

  5. Die-cut window in the flat face, away from the curve.

Comparison with Large Kraft Gift Boxes

The formats sit at opposite ends of the same range. A pillow box is cheap, flat-packed and holds almost nothing; Large Kraft Gift Boxes carry weight, stack and present a set. Collections often use both — pillows for the add-ons and favours, a lidded box for the main product — on one board and one print system.

Print and finishing on a curve

The flat centre panel is the printable area that behaves predictably. Artwork running out towards the curved ends distorts slightly as the box is formed, so type and logos want to stay in the middle third.

Foil works particularly well on the flat face because the shape already reads as decorative, and a sticker seal across the closure doubles as branding and as the thing that stops the ends easing open in a bag.

A pillow box has one dieline and no gluing, so almost the entire cost is the cutting forme and the press run. That means the unit price falls very steeply with quantity — a run of five hundred and a run of five thousand can differ by more than half per box.

It is the reason the format dominates wedding favours, conference giveaways and seasonal promotions, where the count is high and the protection needed is close to zero. For a run of a hundred, a pillow box is rarely the cheapest answer despite being the cheapest box.

Flat-packed they take almost no room, and they open with one push, so a volunteer team can make up several hundred in an evening without training. That practical detail is often what decides the format for an event rather than any packaging consideration.

description:
Kraft Pillow Gift Boxes, Which Hold Their Shape by Tension

A pillow box has no base. It is one flat blank whose curved end scores pull the panels into an arc, and the shape exists only because the board is fighting to lie flat again. At Kraft Box Pack we specify Kraft Pillow Gift Boxes around that tension, because everything that goes wrong with them is the tension being wrong.

Get the board right and the box snaps closed and stays closed with no glue, no tape and no insert. Get it wrong and it either gapes at the ends or refuses to curve at all.

Why board caliper decides everything

Too stiff and it will not curve

Heavy board resists the arc. The ends stay half open, the crimp shows a crease line instead of a clean curve, and the box looks like it failed rather than closed. Pillow boxes want a lighter caliper than a tuck-end box of the same footprint.

Too soft and it will not hold

A board with no spring collapses into a flat envelope the moment the contents settle. The curve goes, the ends splay, and what was a shaped gift box becomes a paper sleeve. The usable window between the two is narrower than most people expect, which is why sampling matters here more than on a square box.

Fill level is part of the specification

A pillow box is the rare pack where how full it is changes how it looks. Overfill it and the arc flattens, the ends are forced apart, and the closure stops holding. Underfill it and the contents slide to one curved end and sit there. There is no flat floor to hold anything in place, so the contents have to roughly match the internal volume rather than simply fit inside it.

Key elements of pillow box design

  1. A caliper light enough to curve and springy enough to hold.

  2. Contents matched to the volume, not merely small enough to fit.

  3. Depth kept shallow, since depth is what fights the arc.

  4. Artwork placed on the flat centre panel, away from the curve.

  5. A ribbon seated in a notch if ribbon is part of the look.

Printing on a surface that moves

The centre of a pillow box is flat and prints normally. Towards the ends the surface curves away, and anything crossing that curve distorts and shortens. Logos, text and any straight rule want to sit inside the flat middle third. Foil and spot UV both sit well there; across the crimp they crack, because the board is still flexing after the box is made.

Comparison with Kraft Heart Shaped Boxes

Both are shaped gift packs that abandon the rectangle, and they solve it in opposite ways. Kraft Heart Shaped Boxes get their shape from a rigid cut wall and a separate lid, so the form is fixed and the contents are free to be any size beneath it. A pillow box gets its shape from the board's own spring, which costs nothing to build but ties the shape to the fill.

Ribbon, and why it slides

A ribbon tied round the middle of a pillow box has nothing to grip. The surface curves away on both sides, so the ribbon migrates towards the widest point and ends up crooked. A pair of small die-cut notches on the long edges fixes it permanently and adds nothing to the unit cost, and it is worth asking for at artwork stage rather than discovering after the first run.

Pillow boxes rarely stand alone. They tend to be the small end of a range, used for the add-on or the favour while a conventional box carries the main item, and the Custom Gift Boxes collection covers what sits alongside them. Running one board stock and one print treatment across both is what makes the pair read as a set.

The dimensions of what goes inside and its weight. From those two we can tell you whether the shape will hold, and if it will not, whether the answer is a lighter board or a shallower box.

Flat blanks stack tightly and take almost no space, which is one of the real advantages of the format. Assembled pillow boxes do the opposite, because the arc that makes them attractive also makes them impossible to nest. Make them up as they are needed rather than in advance.

In transit an assembled pillow box crushes flat under very little load, so anything posted needs an outer carton. The box itself is presentation, not protection.

description:
Kraft Pizza Box Supply Options

A pizza box has about fifteen minutes to solve a problem it cannot fully solve. A pizza leaves the oven at well over 200 degrees and gives off steam the whole way home; trap that steam and the base goes soft, let too much out and the pizza is cold on arrival. At Kraft Box Pack we specify Kraft Pizza Boxes around that balance, because it is the only thing customers actually judge.

Whether you are sourcing kraft pizza boxes wholesale for a delivery kitchen or comparing sizes for a menu, the decisions that matter are the venting, the flute and how the box behaves in a stack.

Benefits of using kraft pizza packaging

Venting, and where the holes go

Small vents let steam escape while keeping most of the heat, and their position matters more than their number. Vents in the side walls release steam without dropping heat the way top vents do. Too many and the pizza cools; too few and the base steams. This is the single specification that decides whether the product arrives as it left.

Corrugated, for insulation as much as strength

The air trapped in the flute is what holds heat, which is why pizza boxes are corrugated rather than folding carton even though the load is light. B flute is the usual choice; E flute prints better but insulates less, and on longer delivery runs that shows.

Grease, which is unavoidable

Pizza is oily and no coating stops that entirely on a hot base. A grease-resistant liner slows it enough that the box does not stain through before delivery, and it keeps the outside clean for the customer's hands. A separate greaseproof liner sheet does the rest.

Stacking is how boxes get crushed

Delivery drivers stack, sometimes six high in a hot bag. The box at the bottom carries the rest, and a lid that dishes touches the cheese. That is where the flute earns its cost: the same box that insulates also has to hold its lid off the food under load. Where orders are routinely multiple pizzas, it is worth specifying for the stack rather than the single box.

Key elements of kraft pizza box design

  1. Side-wall vents, positioned to release steam without heat.

  2. Corrugated flute chosen for insulation and stack strength.

  3. Grease-resistant liner, since oil is a given.

  4. A lid that stays clear of the food under a stack.

  5. Assembly in one motion, because it happens during service.

Shared qualities with Kraft Cookie Boxes

Both are food boxes where the barrier matters more than the board, but the direction is opposite: a pizza box is fighting steam and grease from a hot product, while Kraft Cookie Boxes are protecting something brittle from movement. Pizzerias that also sell baked goods usually need both specifications rather than one shared box.

Important factors in food packaging design

Assembly speed is not a detail here. Pizza boxes are folded during service, often in seconds, and a design that takes four folds instead of two costs real time on a Friday night. It is worth folding a sample by hand before committing to a run.

On print, one or two colours on kraft reads well and survives grease marks better than a full-colour photographic design, which shows every stain. Most of the strongest pizza branding is deliberately simple for exactly that reason.

Recyclable programmes B flute Side-wall vents Water-based coating No plastic lining

Exploring kraft packaging for other foods

Most pizzerias sell sides, desserts and drinks alongside, and the Kraft Packaging Boxes range covers those formats on the same board and print system. Matching them is what makes a delivery order look like one brand rather than three suppliers.

What to send with your enquiry

Your pizza diameters, your average delivery time, and whether orders are usually single or multiple. The first sets the footprint, the second sets the venting, and the third decides the flute.

Sizes, and why menus usually need three

Most pizzerias settle on three footprints and a slice box. Below that, small pizzas rattle and large ones bend to fit; above it, you are holding stock in sizes that turn over slowly. The three should be set from your actual pizza diameters with about an inch of clearance, not from a supplier's standard sizes, because a pizza touching the wall picks up moisture from the board there first.

Choose Kraft Pizza Boxes from Kraft Box Pack, specified against steam rather than against a size chart. We provide:

  • Gloss, matte, and spot UV coating options

  • Free design and free shipping

  • Vent patterns tuned to your delivery times

  • Food-safe and eco-friendly kraft material

  • Fast turnaround times at wholesale rates

Send your pizza sizes and your average delivery time and we will set the venting from both.

faqs.question: What are Kraft POP Display Boxes?
faqs.answer: Kraft POP Display Boxes are countertop display units that hold products in a tray-style layout so items stay visible, grouped, and easy to pick. The structure is generally designed with a straight front edge, stable side walls, and a layout that allows for regular refilling.

faqs.question: What does POP mean in retail display packaging?
faqs.answer: In retail display packaging, POP is a term used for displays placed at the checkout area or in the main buying zone where customers make their selection. POP display packaging is used to position products in a defined space so items remain together, visible, and accessible without requiring additional shelving.

faqs.question: Why do stores use display boxes cardboard structures?
faqs.answer: Stores use cardboard display boxes because they can be shipped flat, take up limited storage space, and can be assembled in the backroom without special tools. Cardboard also allows printing of product information, barcodes, and other details directly on the surface. When an appropriate board grade is selected, the structure can generally withstand routine handling and restocking.

faqs.question: How do I choose the right tray depth for my products?
faqs.answer: Tray depth is usually chosen based on the height and weight of the products. The aim is to keep items upright without leaning backward or falling forward. If the tray is too deep, products can sit too low behind the front edge; if it is too shallow, they may tip when picked up. Checking a sample tray with actual products is a practical way to confirm a suitable depth.

faqs.question: What are custom counter display boxes used for?
faqs.answer: Custom counter display boxes are used to hold and organize small items such as cartons, sachets, pouches, or trial-size packs on counter surfaces. They keep units collected in one defined area instead of spreading loosely across the counter. They are also used when certain products need to be grouped together for a particular period, theme, or range.

faqs.question: What is the difference between a POP tray and a counter stand?
faqs.answer: A POP tray is usually a low-profile tray that holds products in one or more rows at a relatively low height. A counter stand often includes a taller back panel, side wings, or multiple levels for additional product rows or printed information. The choice between the two generally depends on the available counter space, product dimensions, and how the items will be loaded and refilled.

faqs.question: How many products should a POP display hold?
faqs.answer: The number of products a POP display should hold depends on product width, tray depth, and the amount of counter space available. The display is usually planned to look neither empty nor excessively crowded. Many setups use a quantity that aligns with expected sales between refills so the front row can be maintained without overloading the base.

faqs.question: What is a counter display box template?
faqs.answer: A counter display box template is a dieline layout that shows all cut lines, fold lines, locking tabs, tray panels, back panels, and print areas. It acts as the technical plan from which the sheets are cut and creased. A clear template helps ensure that the display folds correctly, supports product weight appropriately, and keeps the front edge and overall shape consistent.

faqs.question: How do custom printed display boxes affect product presentation?
faqs.answer: Custom printed display boxes affect product presentation by providing defined areas for product names, variants, usage information, and other details directly on the display. This makes it easier to distinguish between different products or flavors placed in the same unit. When multiple displays use the same print layout, they create a more uniform appearance across various counters or locations.

faqs.question: Do POP display boxes work for heavier products?
faqs.answer: POP display boxes can be used for heavier products if the base panel, side walls, and folds are specified with suitable board strength and structure. Stronger flute types or thicker boards are often chosen where higher loads are expected. Internal divider lanes can also be included to distribute weight more evenly and keep items in their positions.

faqs.question: How can I keep the display looking neat after refills?
faqs.answer: Keeping the display neat after refills depends on tray depth, side-wall support, and the method used for adding new stock. Many setups use a consistent refill pattern, such as loading from the back or from one side, to keep the front row aligned. A firm front lip helps maintain its shape over time so labels remain visible in a straight line.

faqs.question: What finishes can be used on Kraft POP Display Boxes?
faqs.answer: Typical finishes for Kraft POP Display Boxes include Matte, Gloss, and Spot UV. Matte finish can reduce light reflection under bright store lighting. Gloss finish provides a smoother surface and can make printed areas appear more defined. Spot UV is usually applied to selected parts of the print, such as certain lines or text, where additional contrast or emphasis is needed. The finish is generally selected with handling conditions and cleaning needs in mind.

faqs.question: Are these displays suitable for multi-store rollouts?
faqs.answer: These displays can be used for multi-store rollouts because the same dieline can be repeated and shipped flat to various locations. Consistent sizing and printing keep the display format similar across all stores. When the structure is standardized, staff at different branches can follow the same assembly steps.

faqs.question: How do divider lanes help in POP displays?
faqs.answer: Divider lanes create separate channels within the tray so products remain in distinct rows and do not collapse into each other. This is particularly useful when multiple flavors, variants, or SKUs are displayed together. Divider lanes also make refilling simpler because staff can return products to the same designated spaces each time.

faqs.question: What information should I provide before ordering bulk displays?
faqs.answer: Before ordering bulk displays, it is helpful to provide product dimensions (length, width, height), approximate weight per unit, desired number of facings, and the available counter footprint. It is also useful to specify whether header cards, side wings, or back panels are required, and to share artwork files, color details, and preferred finishes such as Matte, Gloss, or Spot UV. This information is used to set tray depth, base strength, and print zones in line with how the display will be used in stores.

description:
Kraft Popcorn Packaging Boxes, Where the Box Is the Portion

Popcorn is sold by volume, not by weight, which makes the box unusual: it is not holding the portion, it defines it. Change the box and you have changed the product and its margin at the same time. At Kraft Box Pack we treat the sizing of a Kraft Popcorn Packaging Box as a pricing decision as much as a packaging one.

A centimetre of height across a season's trading is a real number in either direction, and it is worth calculating rather than inheriting from whatever size came before.

Almost no weight, a great deal of volume

The board carries nothing

A full popcorn box weighs very little, so caliper is not about load. It is about a box being held, squeezed, carried and set down on a seat arm without buckling — the failures here are handling failures, not structural ones.

It has to stand up empty

A tall box with a light fill tips easily, and it is put down on sloping cinema floors and folding tables. A generous base footprint costs a little more board and prevents most of the spills.

It is carried one-handed

The other hand has a drink in it. That decides the proportions more than anything else: too wide to grip and it gets carried against the body, which is where it gets crushed.

Key elements of popcorn box design

  1. Volume set deliberately, since the box defines the portion.

  2. A base wide enough to stand on an uneven surface.

  3. A grease barrier, because butter reaches the board immediately.

  4. A width that can be held in one hand.

  5. A flat front, since branding is seen while it is carried.

Butter goes through board quickly

Warm butter and popping oil reach uncoated kraft within minutes, and the mark spreads outward from the base until the box is translucent and slippery to hold. A grease-resistant board or an internal coating is required rather than optional on anything buttered. It is a material decision taken before print, and it is the most common reason a first order gets replaced.

Open top, and what that means

Most popcorn boxes have no lid, which removes several problems and creates one: everything about the box is on show, including the inside. A printed or coated interior is visible from the moment it is handed over and stays visible until the box is empty, so it is worth deciding what the inside looks like instead of leaving it as raw board.

Comparison with Kraft Snack Packaging Boxes

Both are impulse food formats and they hold quite different products. Kraft Snack Packaging Boxes usually enclose a portioned, often pre-packed item where weight and shelf life matter, so the pack seals and stacks. A popcorn box is open, served immediately, and specified around volume, grease and being carried in one hand.

Stacking behind the counter

Empty boxes live nested in a stack beside the machine, and the speed of service depends on one coming away cleanly from the next. A taper that is slightly too tight makes them stick together, and a server pulling two at once during a rush is a real cost across an evening. It is worth testing with a full stack rather than a handful.

Popcorn goes stale faster than it looks

Popped corn is mostly surface area, and it takes on moisture from the air within hours. That is fine for immediate service and it is why pre-packed retail popcorn needs a sealed bag inside the carton rather than the carton alone. A printed box around a bag is a different product from a box you pour popcorn into, and mixing the two up is how a retail line arrives soft.

Within a food packaging range

A concession stand needs cups, trays and boxes together, and the Kraft Food Packaging collection covers those formats. One kraft shade and one logo treatment across all of them makes a counter look like a brand rather than a supply cupboard.

What to send with your enquiry

The portion volumes you want to sell and whether the popcorn is buttered or coated. The volumes set the sizes and the topping sets the barrier.

  • Free design and free shipping

  • Grease-resistant boards and printed interiors

  • Food-safe and eco-friendly kraft material

  • Fast turnaround times at wholesale rates

faqs.question: What are kraft popcorn packaging boxes used for?
faqs.answer: Kraft popcorn packaging boxes are used to serve popcorn in a clean, easy-to-hold carton that stays stable on counters. They support quick scooping and sharing without crushing the pack. They’re common for cinemas, kiosks, fairs, stadiums, and event service.

faqs.question: What makes kraft popcorn boxes better for busy counters?
faqs.answer: They stack well, open quickly, and keep their shape during fast handoffs. The base helps reduce tipping on trays and counters. The wide opening supports portioning without slowing the line.

faqs.question: How do I choose the right size for kraft popcorn cartons?
faqs.answer: Start with your serving weight and scoop method. Then select heights that stack neatly in storage and feel comfortable in hand. Keeping two or three portion sizes usually improves speed and reduces confusion.

faqs.question: Can I order custom kraft popcorn boxes in bulk?
faqs.answer: Yes, custom kraft popcorn boxes are often ordered in bulk for repeat programs. Bulk orders work best when the size set and print placement are finalized early. That keeps reorders consistent and storage predictable.

faqs.question: Do you offer printed kraft popcorn boxes?
faqs.answer: Yes, printed kraft popcorn boxes can include logos, patterns, and product messaging. Designs stay cleaner when key text is kept away from folds and corner turns. Balanced margins also help branding look consistent in counter rows.

faqs.question: What finishes are available for kraft popcorn packaging?
faqs.answer: Common finish options include Matte, Gloss, and Spot UV. Matte reduces glare and keeps the kraft tone calm. Gloss adds shine, and Spot UV highlights selected brand areas for contrast.

faqs.question: How can I reduce grease marks on brown kraft popcorn boxes?
faqs.answer: Grease control depends on surface finish choices and portion headroom. A better fit reduces overflow and keeps rims cleaner. Storage stacking and carton packing also matter because pressure can transfer marks between units.

faqs.question: Are kraft popcorn packaging boxes suitable for events and festivals?
faqs.answer: Yes, they’re widely used for events because they’re easy to hold and simple to serve from. They also photograph well in natural lighting. A consistent size family helps staff restock and serve faster during rush windows.

faqs.question: What’s the difference between kraft popcorn cartons and standard paper tubs?
faqs.answer: Kraft popcorn cartons typically offer a firmer structure and a more natural kraft tone. They can feel more stable in hand, especially in stacked service. They also support branding layouts that look clean in counter displays.

faqs.question: Can I get multiple portion sizes in one matching design set?
faqs.answer: Yes, many brands use a matching design set across sizes so the counter line looks uniform. This also helps customers understand small, medium, and large portions quickly. It supports consistent reorders across seasons.

faqs.question: How do I keep cartons from creasing during shipping and storage?
faqs.answer: Use master-carton layouts that reduce movement and rim pressure. Avoid over-tight stacking that crushes edges. Stable footprints and consistent stacking methods keep packs cleaner for service.

faqs.question: Can you help with design and fast production timelines?
faqs.answer: Yes, you can request design support, custom sizes, and fast turnaround scheduling. Keeping dielines and print zones finalized early reduces delays. This is helpful for seasonal runs and event deadlines.

faqs.question: Are kraft popcorn packaging boxes good for branded counter displays?
faqs.answer: Yes, kraft tones support clean branding and consistent presentation. Centered printing and controlled spacing help logos stay readable. Spot UV can add contrast on key areas without covering the full surface.

description:
Kraft PR Packaging Boxes, Where the Box Becomes the Story

A press send goes to somebody who writes for a living and receives dozens of these a week. They are better placed than anyone to notice what the packaging is made of, and increasingly willing to say so. At Kraft Box Pack we specify Kraft PR Packaging Boxes on the assumption that the box itself may be commented on.

A sustainability launch arriving in a plastic-filled box is the classic own goal in this category, and it is written up rather than quietly forgiven.

Three audiences in one parcel

The mailroom

It arrives at a reception desk, is signed for, stacked and carried. If it is enormous or awkward it is resented before anyone sees the brand, and a box too large for a desk is opened somewhere else and abandoned.

The journalist

They open it between other work and need to know within seconds what the product is, what is new about it, and who to contact. That is an information design problem, not a packaging one, but the box is where it is solved.

The camera

Some of these get photographed. Not all, and designing exclusively for that is how the first two audiences get neglected.

Key elements of PR box design

  1. Materials that stand up to being written about.

  2. The story findable in seconds, in print and digitally.

  3. A desk-sized footprint rather than a dramatic one.

  4. A tray that presents the product without wrapping it away.

  5. Contact details attached to the box, not only to the product.

The press release has to survive the unpacking

A card at the bottom of a box under a layer of filler is thrown out with the filler. Whatever carries the story — a printed sheet, a card with a link, a code — belongs at the top, visible on opening, and ideally attached to something rather than loose. It sounds trivial and it decides whether the send generates coverage or a nice product sitting on somebody's desk with no idea who sent it.

Size is a courtesy

Large PR boxes are memorable and they are also a nuisance: they do not fit on a desk, they cannot go in a bin, and they take up a corner of somebody's office until they do. A pack that is generous inside and modest outside earns more goodwill than one built to impress at the door, and it costs less to send.

Comparison with Kraft Subscription Boxes

Both are posted directly to an individual and both are opened away from any shop. Kraft Subscription Boxes repeat monthly to a customer who has already bought in, so the box is fixed and the contents rotate around it. A press box goes once to somebody who has no relationship with the brand yet, so everything — the explanation, the contact, the reason it matters — has to be in that single send.

Small runs, and what that allows

Press lists run to dozens rather than thousands, which makes things possible that a retail line could never justify — a named card, a short-run printed insert, a hand-finished detail. It also means the tooling cost per box is high, so the sensible structure is a simple, well-made box with the money spent on the inside rather than an elaborate construction that has to be paid for across fifty units.

A press send that arrives after the embargo lifts is worthless no matter how well it is made. The schedule runs backwards from the publication date through the send window, the packing, the print and the proof, and it is the one part of this product where a delay cannot be absorbed later. description:
Kraft Promotional Boxes, Designed Before the Contents Exist

Promotional packaging is almost always specified out of order. The campaign is approved, the box is put into production because it has the longest lead time, and the merchandise going inside is still being sourced. At Kraft Box Pack we design Kraft Promotional Boxes knowing that the contents may change after the die is cut.

That is not bad planning so much as the shape of the work, and a box drawn to a tolerance survives it where a box drawn to an exact item does not.

Designing for contents you cannot measure yet

Fix the outer, vary the inner

The printed box carries the long lead time and the artwork approvals. The insert does not. Committing the outer early and leaving the tray until the merchandise is confirmed is what keeps a campaign on schedule.

Give the interior tolerance

A card cradle or a folded divider adapts to a range of sizes. A vacuum-formed tray cut to one exact product does not, and if the supplier substitutes a slightly different item the tray is scrap.

Size from the largest candidate

Where two or three items are still in contention, the box goes to the largest of them. A box that is a little generous can be filled; one that is a little small cannot be stretched.

Key elements of promotional box design

  1. The outer committed early, the insert left until contents are fixed.

  2. An adaptable interior rather than a tray cut to one item.

  3. Sizing taken from the largest item still under consideration.

  4. Artwork checked against the merchandise, not only the brand guide.

  5. A schedule worked back from the campaign date.

The box and the merchandise have to agree

Promotional items are sourced from a different supplier on a different timeline, and the two rarely see each other before they meet in a warehouse. A brand colour that is right on the box and slightly off on the merchandise reads as a mistake, and it is a comparison the recipient makes instantly because both are in their hands at once. Sending a physical sample between the two suppliers is a small step that prevents the most visible failure in this category.

Where the budget actually goes

Promotional packaging is a marketing line, not a cost of goods, and it is scrutinised differently — the question is what the campaign achieved rather than what the unit cost. In practice the money is best spent where the recipient notices it: the interior, the reveal and the printed message. A heavier board rarely registers; a fitted tray and a printed inside almost always do.

Comparison with Kraft Giveaway Packaging Boxes

The two overlap and separate on who chooses the recipient. Kraft Giveaway Packaging Boxes are handed out at events to whoever passes, so the specification is about being wanted and being carryable. A promotional box goes to a chosen list — customers, staff, partners — so it will be accepted regardless, and the design work moves to what is inside it.

Posting to a list

Most promotional boxes are sent rather than handed over, which makes the pack a mailer as well as a presentation. It needs a closure that holds without tape, a shape carriers accept without a surcharge, and a flat area for a label that does not land across the branding. Checking the finished pack against your carrier's dimension bands before the die is cut is worth doing, because a few millimetres can move an entire mailing into a higher price band.

Kraft and the sustainability question

Promotional packaging attracts more scepticism than any other kind, because the recipient did not ask for it. A plain recycled board box with a paper cradle and no plastic answers that criticism before it is made, which is most of why kraft has become the default in this category. The claim has to be true throughout, though — a paper outer with a plastic tray inside undoes the argument entirely.

The campaign date, the send quantity, and the largest item that might go inside. We can commit the outer against those and leave the insert until the merchandise lands.

Kraft Rectangular Gift Boxes Wholesale For Brands

The rectangle is the shape everything else is measured against. It cuts with almost no waste from a sheet, it stacks and ships without air between boxes, and every closure style works on it. At Kraft Box Pack we cut Kraft Rectangular Gift Boxes knowing that the format's advantage is entirely practical — and that the practical advantage is usually worth more than a novelty shape.

Whether you are sourcing rectangular gift boxes wholesale or building a collection, the decisions are the closure, the proportion and whether the interior is printed.

How Rectangular Form Supports Premium Gifting Flow

Nesting and freight

Rectangles tessellate, so a shipping carton or a shelf holds noticeably more of them than of any curved or angled shape. Across a season that is real money, and it is the main reason ranges built on novelty shapes end up adding a rectangle.

Proportion changes the read

A shallow wide rectangle reads as a presentation box. A tall narrow one reads as a bottle or a candle pack. A near-cube reads as neither and is the least distinctive choice. Same material, same cost, entirely different impression — and it is set by two numbers on a dieline.

Every closure works

Lid and base, drawer, magnetic, tuck end and ribbon all suit a rectangle, which means a collection can vary the opening across its range while keeping one footprint and one print system. That is difficult on any other shape.

Sizing a range without waste

Most gift ranges settle on three sizes. Fewer and the small items rattle in boxes too big for them, which reads as cheap however good the board is. More and you are paying for dielines and losing the buying advantage of one long print run. The sizes should come from your actual products rather than from round numbers.

Key elements of rectangular gift box design

  1. Proportion chosen deliberately, since it sets the impression.

  2. Closure matched to how the box should open.

  3. Interior printed, since it is seen at the moment of opening.

  4. Three sizes from your products, not from round numbers.

  5. An insert where the contents would otherwise shift.

Comparison with Kraft Square Gift Boxes

A square is a rectangle that has given up one of its two useful dimensions. Kraft Square Gift Boxes read as neat and self-contained and suit contents that are themselves square; a rectangle suits almost everything else and wastes less space around a product that is longer than it is wide.

Material And Lid Systems For Stable Kraft Builds

Rigid holds a lid tolerance for years and costs several times a folding build. Folding ships flat, costs a fraction and loosens with repeated opening. On a gift box the deciding question is whether the recipient keeps it — a kept box earns rigid, a discarded one does not.

Where the box is posted, the lid is what takes corner crush. A plain outer around it costs far less than reprinting a decorated lid, and it is the difference between arriving square and arriving apologetic.

Print, and how the panels get used

A rectangle gives five printable outside faces and five inside, and most designs use one. The lid top carries the brand, but the long side is what a customer sees when boxes sit on a shelf in a row, and the inside of the lid is what they see at the moment of opening.

Designing all three deliberately costs nothing extra on a print run that is happening anyway. Leaving two of them blank is the most common missed opportunity in gift packaging, and it is visible immediately next to a range that has thought about it.

Colour on a brown ground

Kraft warms and darkens every colour laid on it, and pale shades suffer most because there is not enough pigment to hide the board beneath. A soft pastel can read as beige. Where a palette is fixed and light, a white underbase printed first holds it at the cost of one extra pass — a decision far cheaper to make now than after a proof.

description:
Kraft Ribbon Closure Boxes, and the Knot Nobody Ties Twice

A ribbon is the only closure a customer has to recreate. Every other fastening — a tuck, a magnet, a lock — works the same way on the tenth opening as on the first. A ribbon comes undone and is then re-tied by somebody who is not the person who tied it originally, and it never looks the same again. At Kraft Box Pack we specify Kraft Ribbon Closure Boxes knowing that.

Which means the ribbon has to be anchored to the box rather than merely wrapped around it, or the second opening is the last good one.

Anchoring, and why loose ribbon fails

Wrapped ribbon migrates

A ribbon tied round a box slides towards whichever edge is nearest, ends up off-centre, and works loose in a bag. It looks perfect on the packing bench and rarely arrives that way.

Slots hold it in place

A pair of die-cut slots on each face passes the ribbon through the board, which fixes its position permanently and lets it be re-tied in the same place every time. It adds nothing to the material cost and it is the single change that makes this format work.

A glued anchor is the alternative

Where the design cannot take visible slots, one end can be glued under the lid so only the bow is tied. It halves the work at the packing bench as well.

Ribbon under tension cuts into board

A ribbon pulled tight bears on two edges of the box, and on a light caliper it crushes them into a visible dent within a day. Wider ribbon spreads that load and is the usual fix; the alternative is a heavier board along those edges. Narrow ribbon on a light box is a combination that looks elegant in a drawing and marks the box in reality.

Key elements of ribbon closure design

  1. Slots or a glued anchor, so the ribbon cannot migrate.

  2. Ribbon width chosen against the caliper it bears on.

  3. Sealed ribbon ends, since satin frays from the first cut.

  4. Length calculated for a bow, not for a circumference.

  5. Packing time costed, because tying cannot be rushed.

Choosing the ribbon itself

Grosgrain holds a knot and resists crushing; satin looks richer and slips, so bows loosen; cotton tape suits a plain kraft box and ties easily but creases permanently once folded. Whichever is chosen, cut ends need heat sealing or they fray, and a frayed end is the detail that makes a careful box look careless. It is worth deciding this alongside the board rather than treating it as a finishing touch.

The length people underestimate

Ribbon quantity is calculated from the box's girth plus enough for a bow, and the bow allowance is usually the larger of the two on a small box. Ordering to the girth alone is how a run ends up with ribbon that ties but will not bow, and the shortfall is discovered at the packing bench with a deadline attached.

Comparison with Kraft Shoulder Boxes

Both are presentation formats where the opening is part of the product. Kraft Shoulder Boxes hold their closure through an internal shoulder, so the box opens and closes cleanly with no consumable and nothing to re-tie. A ribbon box trades that reliability for a more generous gesture, and it adds a component that has to be bought, cut and tied every time.

Use Ribbon Anchor Board Notes
Retail gift boxes Grosgrain Slots Medium Re-tied by the customer
Luxury and jewellery Satin Glued end Rigid Wide ribbon, heavy board
Wedding and events Satin Slots Medium Hundreds tied by hand
Artisan food Cotton tape Slots Medium Plain kraft suits it
Posted gifts Grosgrain Glued end Medium Needs an outer carton
Corporate sends Grosgrain Slots Rigid Printed ribbon at volume

What it costs at the bench

Tying is a two-handed job that takes fifteen to thirty seconds and cannot be hurried without looking hurried. Across a few dozen boxes that is nothing; across a thousand it is a person for a day. Where volumes are high the practical answers are a pre-tied bow applied as a unit, or a glued anchor so only one knot is made — both keep the look and remove most of the labour.

Posting a ribboned box

A bow does not survive a courier bag. It is crushed flat, and a flattened satin bow cannot be revived. Anything posted needs an outer carton with enough clearance that nothing presses on the bow, which means the outer is measurably larger than the gift box rather than a snug fit around it.

Within a wider gift range

A ribbon box is usually the top of a range rather than all of it, and the Custom Gift Boxes collection covers the simpler builds beneath. Using one board and one ribbon across the range keeps a mixed order looking like one brand.

What to send with your enquiry

The box dimensions, the ribbon width you want and how many you pack a week. The last figure decides whether slots and hand tying are realistic or whether a pre-tied bow is the better route.

  • Free design and free shipping

  • Food-safe and eco-friendly kraft material

  • Fast turnaround times at wholesale rates

Send your box size and weekly volume and we will work out how the ribbon should be fixed.

description:
Designed for Natural Texture and Modern Aesthetics

A round box is made a completely different way from a square one. There is no dieline and no folding — the wall is wound from a continuous strip of board around a mandrel, and the base and lid are cut discs set into it. That single fact explains most of what follows, including why the tooling is a mandrel diameter rather than a cutting forme, and why changing the height is cheap while changing the diameter is not.

At Kraft Box Pack we wind Kraft Round Boxes to your own diameter and depth. Whether you are sourcing kraft round boxes wholesale or comparing kraft round boxes with lids for a gift range, the diameter is the number to settle first, because everything else adjusts around it.

Why round boxes are preferred for storage

Strength comes from the shape

A cylinder has no corners to crush, which is why the format survives handling that dents a folding carton. The load path runs continuously around the wall instead of concentrating at four vertical creases. That makes a wound tube strong for its weight, and it is the reason posters, spirits and confectionery have used the shape for a century.

What it costs you in freight

The same shape that resists crushing wastes space on a pallet. Circles do not tessellate, so roughly a fifth of the volume between packed cylinders is air you are paying to ship. On a high-value gift item that is irrelevant; on a low-margin bulk product it can outweigh every other saving, and it is worth doing the arithmetic before committing.

Lids, and the fit that makes them feel right

A telescoping lid sliding over the wall gives the slow, cushioned close people associate with a premium pack. The fit depends on the wall thickness being consistent all the way round, which is a winding tolerance rather than a printing one. Too tight and it binds in humidity; too loose and it lifts in a bag.

Printed Kraft Round Boxes with Logo

Printing on a cylinder is not printing on a flat sheet. The artwork is printed on the wrap before it is wound, so the design has to account for the overlap seam where the strip meets itself. A pattern that repeats hides the seam; a single large logo positioned badly runs straight through it.

Where the seam should fall

Decide this at artwork stage. Place the seam at the back of the pack, and put the logo and the mandatory copy on the front third where nothing interrupts them. It costs nothing to plan and cannot be fixed afterwards.

Eco-Friendly Kraft Round Boxes

An unlaminated wound kraft tube with board ends goes into the paper stream intact, which is unusual for a rigid-feeling pack. The thing that breaks it is a metal end cap or a plastic lid — both common, both requiring separation before recycling. Where a recyclability claim matters, board ends keep it true.

Comparison with Kraft Box with Window

A round box hides its contents completely, which suits a product sold on brand rather than on appearance. Where the product needs to be seen, Kraft Box with Window is the better format — a curved window is possible but expensive, because the film has to conform to the wall rather than sit flat.

Sizing and specification

Diameter first, then depth, then lid style. Diameter is the expensive dimension because it is tooling; depth is a cut length and costs almost nothing to change. That is why a range sharing one diameter across three heights is usually far cheaper than three diameters at one height.

description:
Kraft Round Gift Containers, and What a Cylinder Costs

A round container is stronger than a square one of the same board and more expensive to make, and both facts come from the same place. A curved wall carries load all the way around instead of concentrating it at four corners, but it cannot be cut and folded from one flat blank. At Kraft Box Pack we treat Kraft Round Gift Containers as a three-part build, because that is what they are.

A wrapped wall, a base disc and a lid disc, assembled at the factory. That is where the strength comes from and where the cost goes.

Why they cannot ship flat

The wall is already round

A rectangular box is delivered as a stack of blanks and made up on site. A round container is delivered finished, because there is no fold that turns a flat sheet into a cylinder. You are paying to ship air, and the freight on a pallet of round containers is a real line in the cost rather than a rounding error.

Nesting is the only relief

Where a range is designed with graduated diameters, the smaller sizes sit inside the larger ones and a pallet carries several times as much. That has to be designed in from the first drawing — sizes chosen independently will not nest, and retrofitting the idea later means new tooling for every size.

Lid fit moves with the weather

A round lid is held by friction around its whole circumference, with no tuck flap or lock to help. Board takes on moisture in a damp store and gives it up in a dry one, and the diameter moves with it. A lid set tight in a humid factory can bind in a dry showroom; one set loose can fall off. The tolerance is set for the middle of that range, and a lid that is very slightly easy in the warehouse is the safer error.

Key elements of round container design

  1. Diameters chosen so a range nests, decided before tooling.

  2. Lid tolerance set for the damp end of the year, not the dry.

  3. Artwork wrapped, with no detail crossing the wall's seam.

  4. Base disc specified for the load, since it carries all of it.

  5. Freight costed early, because these ship assembled.

Printing on a surface with no front

A cylinder has no natural face. Whatever the artwork does, the customer will pick it up at a random rotation, so a design that depends on one logo in one position is only right a fraction of the time. Repeating patterns and wrapping bands work; a single centred mark works if it is repeated two or three times around the wall. There is also a vertical seam where the wrap closes, and any detail crossing it will step slightly.

Comparison with Kraft Rectangular Gift Boxes

The two are direct alternatives and the trade is straightforward. Kraft Rectangular Gift Boxes ship flat, store flat, print with a defined front and back, and pack efficiently on a shelf. Round containers give up all four of those and return a stronger wall, a more premium feel, and a shape that reads as a gift before it is opened.

Where the interior needs help

A cylinder is an awkward interior. Anything rectangular put inside it leaves four crescent gaps, and the item rotates in transit until it finds a corner. Where the contents are not themselves round, a die-cut disc insert or a wrapped liner is what stops the movement, and it is cheaper to add at the start than to solve with tissue afterwards.

Round containers usually appear alongside conventional boxes rather than instead of them, and the Custom Gift Boxes collection covers what sits beside them. Matching the kraft stock and the print treatment across both is what stops a mixed range looking like two suppliers.

The diameter and height you want, the loaded weight, and whether there will be more than one size. The last question is the one that decides whether the range nests, and it is much cheaper to answer now.

Storage before use

Assembled containers take the room they take, and a graduated range stored nested rather than side by side is the difference between one shelf and four. Keep them dry — the lid fit is the part that notices a damp stockroom first, and a pallet stored against an outside wall will show it before anything else does.
