Long cold storage Aligned vents As crop allows High edge crush Board weakens over days

Produce packaging as a range

Growers and packers run several formats at once, and the Kraft Food Packaging collection covers the trays, punnets and retail builds that sit alongside a field carton. Standardising the footprint across them is what makes palletising straightforward.

What to send with your enquiry

The crop, how long it is stored and at what temperature, and your pallet configuration. The first sets the venting and fill depth, the second sets the board, the third fixes the footprint.

Recycled content and wet strength

Produce cartons are among the most recycled packaging in use, and most are made largely from recycled fibre. The trade is real: recycled liners have shorter fibres and less wet strength, which matters more here than almost anywhere because these boxes live damp for days at a time.

Where a stack is high or storage is long, testing the actual grade at the actual humidity is worth doing rather than trusting a dry figure. The difference between a stack that holds and one that slumps is often a single grade.

Washing, reuse and returnable systems

Some supply chains run returnable plastic crates instead, and the comparison is worth making honestly. Crates win on repeated use and lose on weight, cleaning cost and the logistics of getting them back. Board wins where the journey is one-way, which most produce journeys are.

Printing on a wet carton

Inks and coatings have to tolerate condensation without lifting, which rules out finishes that would be fine on a dry-goods box. Most field cartons carry a simple one or two colour flexo print for that reason, with the detail reserved for retail-facing builds.

description:
Kraft Watch Packaging Boxes, Which Are Kept

Almost all packaging is thrown away within a minute of arriving. A watch box is not — it goes into a drawer and holds the watch on the nights it is not worn, sometimes for years. At Kraft Box Pack we specify Kraft Watch Packaging Boxes as a small piece of furniture rather than as a carton, because that is how they are actually used.

That changes what matters. The hinge has to survive hundreds of openings, and the interior has to be kind to a crystal for a very long time.

The strap is the difficult part

Leather must not be stored flat

A leather strap laid flat creases across the lug, and the crease becomes permanent within weeks. That is why a watch box has a cushion — the strap wraps around it and holds the curve it will take on the wrist, which is the shape the leather should be resting in.

Metal bracelets behave differently

A bracelet has no memory to protect, but it has weight and it scratches. Curved over a cushion it stays clear of the box's own walls, which is the point on a metal band.

Cushion diameter is not decorative

Too thin and the strap is still bent tight; too thick and the strap will not close around it, so the watch sits loose and moves. It is sized to the strap length, not to the box.

What touches the crystal

Anything harder than the interior lining will eventually mark the glass, and in a box that is opened repeatedly for years, eventually arrives. The seat wants a soft-touch lining, and any structural board underneath it wants covering rather than exposing. A rough kraft edge sitting where the case rests is the sort of detail that looks fine on the first day and is visible on the watch a year later.

Key elements of watch box design

  1. A cushion sized from the strap, not from the box.

  2. A soft lining wherever the case or crystal can touch.

  3. A hinge rated for years of use, not for one opening.

  4. Room for the papers, since a warranty card is part of the sale.

  5. An outer shipper, because the box is not the transit pack.

The paperwork has to live somewhere

A watch is sold with a warranty card, an instruction booklet and often a spare link or two, and all of that has to travel with the box or it is lost. A slot in the lid, a compartment beneath the cushion or a document sleeve is the difference between a complete watch in five years and a watch with no papers. On resale that difference is money, and customers know it.

Comparison with Kraft Ring Packaging Boxes

Both are jewellery boxes designed to be kept, and the difference is what the interior has to do. Kraft Ring Packaging Boxes grip a small hard object in a slot, so the interior is a clamp and the box can be tiny. A watch box holds a long flexible strap in a curve and a heavy case above it, so the interior is a form rather than a grip, and the footprint is set by the strap.

Never ship it as its own parcel

A watch box posted bare arrives with a courier label across the lid and corner damage on a product the customer intends to keep. It needs a plain outer carton with enough void fill that the presentation box does not move, and the cost of that outer is trivial against the box it is protecting.

Kraft in a category built on black

Watch packaging is overwhelmingly black, and a brown kraft box reads as deliberate against it — craft, independent, unpolished on purpose. It works well with foil and with blind embossing, and it works badly with anything trying to look expensive in the conventional way. The material is a positioning choice more than a cost one, and it should be made for that reason.

Within a jewellery range

Watches usually sit alongside other accessories rather than alone, and the Jewelry & Accessories Boxes collection covers the boxes around them. Sharing a lining and a finish across the range is what makes a counter display look like a single brand.

The case diameter, the full strap length and the case weight. The strap sets the footprint, the diameter sets the cushion, and the weight decides the hinge.

description:
Kraft Wax Melt Boxes, and the Product That Changes State

A wax melt is solid on the shelf and liquid in a warm van, and the box has to be right in both conditions. Nothing else in cosmetics packaging has that problem quite so plainly. At Kraft Box Pack we specify Kraft Wax Melt Boxes for the warm case first, because the cool case looks after itself.

Uncoated kraft and melted fragrance oil are a poor combination. Once the wax softens and touches bare board, the oil wicks straight into the fibre and the stain never comes out.

Three things the box has to survive

Heat softening the product

Soy and paraffin blends start to give up their shape well below the temperature a delivery van reaches in summer. A clamshell or a sealed tray between the wax and the board is what keeps the box saleable, and where the melt sits directly in the box, the board needs a barrier coating rather than a print finish.

Fragrance oil migrating

Scent moves through paperboard. Left long enough, a strongly fragranced melt will scent the box, then the carton it sits in, then everything on the shelf beside it — which is how a range of six fragrances ends up smelling like one. A barrier board or a sealed inner wrap is the only real fix.

Snapping into segments

Most melts are sold as a scored bar that the customer breaks apart. That means the pack is opened, part-used and closed again several times, so a tuck end that survives repeated opening is worth more here than on a pack that is opened once.

Key elements of wax melt box design

  1. A barrier between wax and board, coated or as a clamshell.

  2. Fragrance containment, so a range does not blend on the shelf.

  3. A closure that still holds after the tenth opening.

  4. Fragrance name legible at a glance across a full display.

  5. Space reserved for CLP and allergen information at artwork stage.

The label the law requires

Fragranced products carry mandatory safety information — hazard wording, allergen declarations and the responsible person's details — and it takes more room than anyone allows for. Designing the pack first and finding somewhere for the text afterwards is how the compliance panel ends up crammed onto a side face at five point. Block the space out at the start, and it stops being a problem.

Selling a scent you cannot smell

A closed box hides the one attribute the customer is buying. Some brands answer that with a window, which reintroduces the migration problem; most answer it with the name and the colour, which is why fragrance names on a wax melt pack want to be large and easy to tell apart at arm's length. A range of six that reads as six is worth more shelf turnover than a range of six that reads as one.

Comparison with Kraft Candle Sleeve Boxes

Both hold scented wax and the fragrance problem is shared, but the load case is not. Kraft Candle Sleeve Boxes wrap a rigid vessel that carries its own weight, so the sleeve is presentation and the glass does the work. A wax melt box is holding the product directly, which puts the oil, the heat and the repeated opening all onto the board.

Storage, and the summer problem

Stock held in a loft, a garage or a van overnight sees temperatures nothing on the shelf ever does, and wax that has melted and reset once will have distorted, leaked or lost its scoring. That damage happens in storage rather than in transit, so where a business holds stock over a summer, the storage conditions matter more to the finished product than the courier does.

Flat blanks are unaffected by any of that, so ordering boxes ahead is safe even where making the product ahead is not.

description:
Large Kraft Gift Boxes, Where Span Becomes the Problem

Scale up a gift box and nothing scales with it evenly. The contents get heavier, the panels get longer and start to bow, and the lid becomes something two hands are needed for. At Kraft Box Pack we specify Large Kraft Gift Boxes around the unsupported span, because that is what changes when a box gets big.

Whether you are sourcing large gift boxes wholesale for hampers or bulky products, the numbers that matter are the longest panel, the loaded weight and whether anyone has to carry it.

What changes at size

Panels bow

A board that holds a small box rigid will flex visibly across a long panel. Compensating means a heavier caliper, moving to corrugated, or breaking the span with an internal tray — and the tray is usually the cheapest of the three.

Lids rack

A long lid can twist very slightly out of square and then bind on one corner permanently. Equal spans resist that; long rectangles need a tighter tolerance and a stiffer board to stay true.

Weight lands on the base

A loaded large box is lifted from underneath, and the base carries everything. A full-overlap base spreads that; a single glued seam is where large boxes fail, always at the moment of lifting.

Carrying, and when a handle becomes necessary

Past roughly a foot square, a box becomes awkward to hold flat and people tilt it. On a gift that is the failure — contents shift, ribbon slides, presentation goes. A die-cut handle or a ribbon carry keeps it level and costs very little against the alternative.

Key elements of large gift box design

  1. Caliper chosen from the longest panel, not the contents.

  2. An internal tray to break a long span, where possible.

  3. Full-overlap base, since the load is lifted from below.

  4. A handle or ribbon carry above about a foot square.

  5. Freight costed early, because large boxes ship expensively.

Comparison with Kraft Candle Boxes

Both are weight problems and at different scales. Kraft Candle Boxes concentrate a kilogram onto a small base, so the base construction matters and the panels never bow. A large gift box spreads less weight over much longer spans, so the panels are the issue and the base is easier. Same principle, opposite geometry.

Shipping, which is the real cost

Carriers charge on dimensional weight, and a large gift box is mostly air by that measure. Where these are posted rather than collected, the freight can exceed the box, and it is worth checking before a size is fixed — an inch off each dimension sometimes moves a parcel into a cheaper band.

Flat-packed delivery helps at the supply end, but an assembled large box takes a great deal of storage, so ordering to a schedule rather than in one annual run is usually more practical.

Large boxes within a range

A large box is usually the top of a family rather than all of it, and the Kraft Gift & Specialty Boxes collection covers the smaller builds beneath it. Sharing one board and print system is what makes a three-size range read as one, and it keeps the largest box from looking like a different product.

What to send with your enquiry

The longest dimension, the loaded weight, and whether anyone carries it by hand. The first sets the material, the second the base, the third whether you need a handle.

Assembly, and the space it needs

Large boxes are delivered flat and made up on site, and a large flat blank needs a large flat surface to fold on. That sounds obvious and it is regularly the problem — a stockroom with no clear bench turns a two-minute job into an awkward one, and boxes get assembled badly.

Where a range sells in bursts, the practical route is to keep the blanks flat and make up a day's worth at a time, since an assembled large box takes several times the storage of a flat one.

Inserts that do structural work

On a large box an insert is not only presentation. A tray dividing the interior braces the long panels from inside, which lets a lighter board hold its shape and saves more than the tray costs. Specifying the two together usually gives a better box than specifying either alone.

Ribbon at scale

A ribbon that looks generous on a small box looks mean on a large one, and the length needed grows faster than the box does. Where ribbon is part of the design, checking the quantity against the largest size in a range avoids ordering three times and finding out.

Choose Large Kraft Gift Boxes from Kraft Box Pack, specified for the span rather than the contents. We provide:

  • Gloss, matte, and spot UV coating options

  • Free design and free shipping

  • Internal trays that stiffen a long panel

  • Food-safe and eco-friendly kraft material

  • Fast turnaround times at wholesale rates

Wholesale Mini Kraft Boxes for Packaging

At small sizes the economics invert. Board costs almost nothing, and the dieline, the plates and the press setup cost the same as they would for a box ten times the size — so on a mini box you are buying tooling and a print run rather than material. At Kraft Box Pack we cut Mini Kraft Boxes to your dimensions with that in mind, because the levers that make them cheap are quantity and shared tooling.

Whether you are sourcing mini kraft boxes wholesale for samples or favours, the two decisions that move the price are how many sizes you need and how many of each you order.

Why Mini Kraft Boxes are important

Fit shows more at this scale

A five millimetre gap around a large product is invisible; around a small one it is a third of the box. Contents that rattle read as cheap immediately, which is why mini boxes are specified to the product far more tightly than larger formats.

Lighter board is genuinely enough

Panel spans are short, so there is little for the board to bow across. A lighter caliper holds its shape perfectly at this size and feels no worse in the hand. It is one of the few real savings available here that costs nothing in quality.

Print has a floor

Fine type and hairline rules that work on a large carton vanish on a small panel, and uncoated kraft spreads ink slightly into the fibre, which costs another fraction of legibility. Setting type a size larger than feels necessary is the usual fix, and testing a printed proof at actual size is the only reliable check.

Assembly, multiplied by the count

Mini boxes are ordered in high quantities and assembled by hand, so a shape that takes three seconds instead of one adds hours across a run of several thousand. Folding a sample before ordering is worth more here than on any other format, because the time cost scales with the count.

Key elements of mini box design

  1. Sized tightly to the product, since gaps show.

  2. Lighter caliper, because panel spans are short.

  3. Type set larger than the design suggests.

  4. Quick assembly, since the count is high.

  5. Several sizes sharing one board and one print run.

Comparison with Kraft Candy Boxes

Where the contents are food, the specification changes rather than the size. Kraft Candy Boxes add a barrier chosen against sugar or chocolate — moisture in one direction, fat in the other — which a plain mini box does not carry. A small box holding confectionery is a food pack first and a small box second.

Making a short run affordable

The unit price falls steeply from a few hundred to a couple of thousand, then flattens. Digital printing removes the plate cost and suits the short end; offset costs more to set up and less per unit once volumes climb. Asking for both rather than assuming one is worth doing, because the crossover depends on how many colours the design uses.

Mini Kraft Boxes for Retail and Gifts

Small boxes are almost always part of a set rather than the whole of it, and the Kraft Gift & Specialty Boxes collection covers the larger lidded, drawer and window builds they normally sit beside. Ordering them together is what makes a range look like a range.

What to send with your enquiry

The product dimensions, how many sizes you need, and the total quantity across all of them. At this scale the total quantity moves the unit price far more than anything about the box.

Where a mini box is the wrong answer

Two cases come up repeatedly. The first is a product that needs to stand upright and does not — at this scale a box has little internal structure, so anything top-heavy needs a fitment rather than a smaller box. The second is anything posted on its own: a mini box has almost no crush resistance and arrives dented, so it belongs inside something else.

Both are cheaper to solve at the specification stage than to discover after a run of five thousand. Describing what the box has to survive, rather than only what goes in it, usually surfaces them.

Finishes that suit the size

Foil and emboss read well on a small box because the whole surface is close to the eye, and they cost less here than on a large format simply because there is less area to cover. Full-colour photographic print is the opposite — it needs space to work and rarely justifies itself at this size.

  • Fast turnaround times at wholesale rates
